title: Baseline retest for cores/bench
Iterative radix-2 divider off the EX critical path + single shared 33x33 multiplier
motivation:
Fmax is 5.442 MHz. The worst path (199.8 ns, 156 cells) is
clock -> u_fwd -> u_ex -> u_ex/u_alu -> u_ex: forwarding mux, then the
fully combinational 32-bit `/` and `%` in alu.sv (DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU,
about 32 chained 32-bit subtract/mux stages, built twice for signed and
unsigned), then the EX/MEM register. Every other EX path is a fraction
of that length, so the divider alone caps the score at about 12 iter/s.
CoreMark's timed region (list/matrix/state/crc kernels at -O3) has
almost no integer divides; the divides are in init and reporting code
outside the start/stop markers. A multi-cycle divider therefore costs
close to zero in iterations/cycle and removes the dominant path. The
combinational divider is also most of the 12.3k LUT4 count. Next, alu.sv
builds three separate 32x32->64 multipliers (ss, uu, su). Once the
divider is gone they will probably be the next limiter and use most of
the DSP blocks. One 33x33 signed multiplier covers all four MUL ops.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
1. Remove the combinational DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU arms from alu.sv in the
   real-arithmetic (non-ALTOPS) build. Add a new module
   rtl/divider.sv: a radix-2 restoring divider that works on unsigned
   magnitudes and produces one quotient bit per cycle (32 iterations).
   - Inputs: clock, reset, start, op (is_signed, is_rem), a, b.
     Outputs: busy, done, result.
   - On start, latch |a|, |b| (two's-complement negate when signed and
     the sign bit is set), q_neg = (a[31]^b[31]) & signed & (b != 0),
     r_neg = a[31] & signed, and the is_rem selector.
   - Each cycle: {rem,quo} <<= 1; trial = rem - |b| (33-bit); if no
     borrow, rem = trial and quo[0] = 1.
   - Finish: result = is_rem ? (r_neg ? -rem : rem)
                             : (q_neg ? -quo : quo).
     The spec corner cases fall out of the plain algorithm: x/0 gives
     quo = 0xFFFFFFFF and rem = |a|. q_neg is forced to 0 when b == 0, so
     DIV-by-0 gives -1 and REM-by-0 gives a. INT_MIN/-1 gives
     |a| = 0x80000000, quo = 0x80000000, and negating keeps 0x80000000,
     rem = 0. No extra wide comparators are needed except b == 0.
   - The critical path per cycle is one 33-bit subtract plus a 2:1 mux,
     starting at flops. That is far shorter than the remaining EX paths.
2. Connect the divider in ex_stage.sv. Let is_div = in.valid &&
   alu_op in {DIV, DIVU, REM, REMU}, using a 1-bit predecode flag
   (ctrl.is_div) set in decoder.sv so EX does not need a wide compare.
   - The divider starts on the first cycle the div sits in EX. It
     latches the post-forwarding rs1/rs2 at that moment, so later
     forwarding changes cannot corrupt it.
   - ex_busy = is_div && !div_done.
   - While ex_busy: the EX/MEM register captures a bubble (valid = 0,
     reg_write = 0, mem_read/mem_write = 0, so nothing retires twice),
     the ID/EX register holds, and the PC holds.
   - When done, EX/MEM captures the divider result as alu_result. The
     divider returns to idle only when EX/MEM actually advances
     (!stall_ex_mem), so a dmem stall coinciding with completion does
     not lose or restart the op.
3. Add ex_busy to hazard_unit.sv: stall_if |= ex_busy;
   stall_id |= ex_busy; flush_id &= !ex_busy. The new stall_ex_mem
   behavior is "bubble on ex_busy, hold on dmem_stall". dmem_stall
   keeps priority: hold everything, and the divider keeps iterating,
   which is harmless.
4. Formal (ALTOPS) consistency: under `RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS` the
   divider keeps the same start/busy/done handshake but finishes after
   about 2 cycles. Its result is the existing ALTOPS stand-in formula,
   (a - b) ^ const, computed from the latched operands. The constants
   are unchanged. The stall, bypass and retirement logic of a multi-cycle
   op is then still proved by riscv-formal, and the liveness check
   (next retirement within 10 cycles of the trigger at depth 20) still
   passes. A 32-cycle latency under ALTOPS would fail liveness.
5. Multiplier: replace mul_ss, mul_uu and mul_su with one product,
   prod = $signed({a[31] & a_sgn, a}) * $signed({b[31] & b_sgn, b}),
   where a_sgn = op in {MULH, MULHSU} and b_sgn = op == MULH. MUL reads
   prod[31:0]; MULH, MULHSU and MULHU read prod[63:32]. One 33x33 array
   replaces three 32x32 arrays. Gowin maps it to a single MULT36X36
   cascade, cutting DSP count and fan-in to the ALU result mux. The
   ALTOPS arms stay as they are.
Measured during hypothesis generation (`make timing TARGET=bench`,
Gowin place_option 0, edit since reverted). The experiment stubbed the
four div/rem arms to 0 and folded the three products into one
sign-extended product.
- Fmax: 50.017 MHz, up from 5.442 MHz (9.2x).
- Area: logic 1983 (down from about 12.3k), 460 registers, DSP 2.
- New worst path: 25.3 ns, 20 logic levels. It runs from a regfile
  LUT-RAM read through the EX branch compare and redirect, into
  if_stage, hazard_unit (stall/flush), and ends at ID/EX.rs2_val and
  the PC register. The merged multiplier is not on the top-5 paths.
The real iterative divider adds only a 33-bit subtract per cycle
between flops, plus one ex_busy term in the stall/flush logic. Fmax
should therefore land close to the measured 50 MHz. CoreMark
iterations/cycle should be essentially unchanged because the timed
loop has very few divides. Expected fitness is about 12.1 -> 100+
iter/s. The +50 below is only the schema cap, not the estimate.
Implementation note: keep ex_busy off the redirect path. It should
only OR into stall_if/stall_id and the EX/MEM bubble select, and it
should be computed from registered state (ID/EX.ctrl.is_div plus the
divider's done flop), not from forwarded operands.

The b==0 quotient-sign override gives the RV32M results for divide-by-zero and INT_MIN/-1 without extra wide compares. Under RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS, the same handshake finishes after about 2 cycles and returns the existing (a-b)^const stand-ins from the latched operands.

lesson: - 2026-10-01 hyp-20261001-001-r1s0 (improvement, +789.85%): The combinational `/` and `%` in alu.sv capped Fmax at 5.4 MHz and used most of the LUTs, and CoreMark's timed loop has almost no divides, so a 32-cycle radix-2 divider that stalls IF/ID through a registered `ex_busy` cost almost no IPC and raised Fmax about 9x (under ALTOPS it must finish in about 2 cycles or riscv-formal liveness fails).

title: Take M-ext out of the 1-cycle EX ALU: MEM-stage pipelined DSP multiplier + iterative radix-2 divider
motivation:
Baseline Fmax is 5.442 MHz. The reported worst path (199.8 ns, 156 cells)
is clock -> u_fwd -> u_ex -> u_ex/u_alu -> u_ex, i.e. the forwarding mux
feeding the fully combinational 32-bit `/` and `%` operators (signed and
unsigned DIV/REM, each a ~32-level ripple-subtract array) plus three
64-bit `*` products, all crammed into the single EX cycle. Every other
path in a textbook 5-stage RV32I pipeline (fwd mux -> 32-bit add/shift/
compare -> EX/MEM, branch compare -> redirect -> PC) should be in the
15-25 ns range on GW2A, so the divider alone costs roughly 8-10x in
clock frequency. It is also most of the 12.3k LUT4 count. CoreMark's
timed loop executes very few DIV/REM (none in list/matrix/state kernels)
but a fair number of MULs (matrix_mul_* kernels), so the right structure
is: cheap low-latency pipelined multiply, slow-but-tiny iterative divide.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Restructure the M-extension datapath so that no M-ext arithmetic sits in
the single-cycle EX ALU:

1. MULTIPLY -> 2-stage pipelined, load-like. In EX, a MUL/MULH/MULHSU/
   MULHU only latches its post-forward operands (sign-extended to 33 bits
   per op: a signed for MULH/MULHSU, b signed for MULH only) plus a
   hi/lo select into the EX/MEM register (reuse rs1_val/rs2_val fields
   or add dedicated mul_a/mul_b fields). In MEM, a single 33x33 signed
   multiply (maps onto Gowin DSP MULT blocks) is computed from those
   registered operands and the selected 32-bit half is written into
   MEM/WB.read_data (treated like a load result: mem_to_reg-style mux,
   so WB/forwarding see it through the existing MEM/WB path). The
   hazard unit's load-use check is extended to "id_ex is a load OR a
   multiply" so a dependent instruction directly behind a MUL gets one
   bubble; MUL throughput stays 1/cycle and independent MULs cost
   nothing. The EX/MEM->EX forward of alu_result is never used for a
   MUL (blocked by the interlock), exactly as for loads. dmem stall
   behaviour is unchanged (EX/MEM holds, MEM/WB keeps data for fwd).

2. DIVIDE/REMAINDER -> new rtl/muldiv.sv (or div_unit.sv) iterative
   radix-2 restoring divider, ~33-34 cycles. Start when a valid DIV/
   DIVU/REM/REMU is in ID/EX and the unit is idle: latch |a|, |b|,
   sign flags, op, and also latch the post-forward rs1/rs2 values
   (CRITICAL: while the divider runs, EX/MEM receives bubbles, so the
   instructions the operands were forwarded from drain out of EX/MEM
   and MEM/WB; the ID/EX rs?_val copy is stale, so both the arithmetic
   and the RVFI rs1_rdata/rs2_rdata must come from the latched copy).
   While busy: assert ex_busy -> stall_if, stall_id (hold, not flush),
   EX/MEM captures a bubble (valid=0, reg_write=0, mem ops=0). When
   done: EX/MEM captures the div result in alu_result with the latched
   operands as rs1_val/rs2_val; the unit goes idle only once EX/MEM has
   actually accepted the result (respect stall_ex_mem/dmem_stall).
   RV32M corner cases: b==0 -> quotient all-ones (do NOT apply sign
   fixup), remainder = dividend; INT_MIN/-1 falls out of the unsigned
   magnitude algorithm + sign fixup naturally (q=0x80000000, r=0) but
   add an explicit check to be safe. A redirect can never coincide with
   a div in EX (div does not branch), but a redirect from an older
   instruction is impossible too since EX is in-order; still gate start
   on in.valid.

3. ALTOPS: under `ifdef RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS keep the exact same
   substitution formulas, computed in the same places (MEM-stage mul
   path from the registered operands; divider "result" from latched
   operands) and give the divider a short fixed latency (e.g. 2 cycles)
   in ALTOPS mode so the stall/hold handshake is still exercised by
   formal but stays well inside the depth-20 BMC / liveness windows.

alu.sv keeps only the RV32I ops (ADD/SUB/logic/SLT/shift/LUI), so the
EX critical path becomes fwd mux -> 32-bit adder/shifter/comparator ->
EX/MEM or -> redirect -> PC. Expected Fmax: ~45-70 MHz (8-12x), area
drops by several thousand LUT4. IPC cost: +1 cycle only for MUL with
an immediately dependent consumer, and ~33 cycles per DIV/REM, which
are essentially absent from CoreMark's timed region -> estimated
CoreMark/MHz loss < 5%. Net fitness expected far above +50% (schema
cap), i.e. roughly 12 -> 80-120 iter/s.

title: IF-stage BTB + 2-bit BHT so correctly predicted taken branches/jumps cost 0 bubbles
motivation:
Every taken BRANCH, JAL and JALR currently resolves in EX and costs a
2-cycle bubble (IF and ID are flushed; the redirect target is only
fetched the next cycle). The core always predicts "not taken / pc+4".
Measured on the baseline cosim (coremark.elf, --istall --dstall,
2.94M retired insns, 4.51M cycles, CPI 1.54): BRANCH = 18.1% of insns
with 10.1% of insns being taken branches, JAL = 1.7%, JALR = 0.5%.
So ~12.3% of instructions pay a 2-cycle redirect = ~0.25 CPI (16% of
all cycles). A trace-driven model of the proposed predictor (64-entry
direct-mapped, full tag, 2-bit ctr, allocate-on-taken) gives 331k
correctly-predicted taken CF vs 23.7k false-taken and 1.3k wrong
target: net 615k cycles saved = 13.6% of cycles (~+15.8% IPC); 32
entries -> 13.4%, 128 entries -> 13.9%, so 64 is the knee. Fmax (5.44 MHz) is set by the
~200 ns combinational divider path fwd->EX->ALU->EX/MEM, so small,
shallow fetch-side logic is free in Fmax terms: any CPI saved converts
1:1 into fitness.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a small direct-mapped branch target buffer with per-entry 2-bit
saturating counters, looked up combinationally from the PC register in
IF, and turn the EX-stage redirect into a "mispredict" redirect.

Predictor (new module rtl/branch_predictor.sv):
  - 64 entries, indexed by pc[7:2]; each entry = {tag pc[19:8] (12b),
    target[31:2] (30b), ctr (2b)} kept in an inferred distributed
    LUT-RAM (sync write, async read); a 64-bit valid vector in flops,
    cleared on reset (so no X/uninitialised reads in sim/formal).
  - Lookup: hit = valid[idx] && tag match; pred_taken = hit && ctr[1];
    pred_target = {target, 2'b00}.
  - Update (one write port, from the EX stage, only for a valid,
    non-faulting BRANCH/JAL/JALR when EX is not stalled):
      taken/jump -> write {tag, actual target, ctr = hit ? sat_inc(ctr)
                    : 2'b10 (weakly taken)}, set valid;
      not-taken  -> if the entry hits, write sat_dec(ctr).
    JAL becomes effectively 100% predicted after first execution; JALR
    gets "last target" prediction (monomorphic call sites / returns).
    Misaligned-target traps never allocate.

IF (if_stage.sv): next_pc = redirect ? redirect_target
                           : pred_taken ? pred_target : pc + 4.
Priority unchanged: reset > redirect > stall > advance. The prediction
(pred_taken, pred_next_pc) is emitted on the IF/ID bundle alongside
pc/instr in the SAME cycle it is used to advance the PC, so the bit that
travels down the pipe always matches the path actually fetched (BTB
writes between a held cycle and the advancing cycle are harmless).

ID (id_stage.sv / core_pkg.sv): add pred_next_pc (32b) to if_id_t and
id_ex_t; flushed/bubbled entries carry valid=0.

EX (ex_stage.sv): actual_next = misalign_fault ? pc+4
   : is_jump ? jump_target : branch_taken ? branch_target : pc+4
(this already exists as the pc_next value). New
   redirect = in.valid && (actual_next != in.pred_next_pc);
   redirect_target = actual_next.
i.e. redirect fires only on a misprediction (wrong direction, wrong
target, or a BTB alias hitting a non-control-flow instruction). A
correctly-predicted taken branch now costs 0 bubbles instead of 2; a
false "taken" prediction on a not-taken branch costs the same 2 as
today's taken branch. The EX/MEM pc_next / RVFI fields are unchanged
(they already carry the architectural next PC), so pc_fwd/pc_bwd and
every other riscv-formal check see the same architectural trace. The
hazard/flush logic is unchanged — it already keys off `redirect`.
To keep the redirect compare off the forwarding path as much as
possible, the implementer may split it as
   (pred_taken != (branch_taken|is_jump)) ||
   (actual_taken && pred_target != target)

title: Squash wrong-path fetch by valid/ctrl gating only: take EX redirect off the IF-instr -> hazard -> ID/EX-enable path
motivation:
The champion (r1s0, 48.4 MHz, 27.3 ns, 21 logic levels) and r1s1 are both
limited by the same path: clock -> u_id -> u_ex -> u_if -> u_hazard -> u_id
(ends at ID/EX rs2_val). EX resolves a branch/jump (forward mux -> 32-bit
compare -> redirect). Then redirect does three things in series:
  (1) in if_stage it muxes the IF/ID instruction to a NOP (32-bit mux),
  (2) the muxed rs1/rs2 fields go to the hazard unit's load-use compare and
      to the regfile read addresses / decoder / imm_gen,
  (3) load_use and redirect drive stall_id and flush_id, which are the
      CE/SR of all ~200 ID/EX flops (high fanout), plus stall_if.
Steps (1)-(3) are not needed for correctness. A wrong-path instruction
only has to reach ID/EX with valid=0 and its side-effect bits cleared.
The register indices, immediate and decode do not need to be NOPs.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Squash the wrong-path instruction with a few gated bits instead of
rewriting it into a NOP:
  - if_stage: out.instr = imem_data always (drop the NOP mux). out.valid
    stays !(flush || redirect).
  - core/hazard: the load-use compare and the regfile read addresses use
    the raw fetched rs1/rs2 fields. Remove `redirect` from flush_id:
    flush_id = load_use_hazard && !dmem_stall. A spurious load-use seen
    during a redirect or imem-stall cycle is harmless. In that cycle the
    ID/EX capture is a bubble anyway, and redirect already has priority
    over stall in the PC register.
  - id_stage: at ID/EX capture, AND the side-effect control bits with
    in.valid: reg_write, mem_read, mem_write, is_branch, is_jump, is_jalr
    and is_div. Then a wrong-path or imem-stalled instruction captured
    with valid=0 cannot redirect, write the regfile, forward, touch
    dmem, start the divider or trigger a later load-use stall.
After the change, redirect fans out only to the PC next-state mux and
about 8 ID/EX D-inputs, each through one LUT. The hazard unit,
stall_if/stall_id/flush_id, the regfile read addresses, the decoder
and imm_gen then depend only on registers and the fetched word
(imem_data is a registered source in the FPGA bench). This removes
about 5-8 logic levels and a high-fanout CE/SR net from the 21-level
critical path. The next limiter should be ID/EX -> forward mux ->
branch compare -> redirect -> PC (or the EX ALU/DSP -> EX/MEM path),
roughly 14-15 levels. The cycle behavior is unchanged: the same
instructions retire in the same cycles. CPI is the same and the gain is
all Fmax. Expected Fmax is about 58-65 MHz, against 48.4 MHz now.

title: Break both 27 ns twin paths: decouple EX redirect from ID/hazard, give dmem its own AGU, move MUL to an EX->MEM 2-stage DSP
motivation:
I ran `make timing` on r1s0 (the champion, 45-48 MHz). It shows two
critical paths with almost the same slack (-17.02 ns and -16.98 ns at
a 5 ns target), so fixing only one of them gains nothing. That
explains r1s1, which moved MUL out of EX and still got no Fmax.
 (A) Redirect loop. Gowin retimes the ID/EX rs?_val register in front
     of the LUT-RAM regfile, so the async regfile read sits in EX. The
     path is regfile DO -> write-first bypass -> 3-level forward mux ->
     32-bit compare carry chain -> redirect -> u_if NOP mux on the
     IF/ID instruction -> u_hazard load-use compare -> u_id stall/flush
     -> CE/RESET of every ID/EX and PC flop (paths 1-5, 7-14, 18-25).
 (B) Multiplier into the dmem address. Gowin absorbs
     EX/MEM.alu_result into the dmem BSRAM address register (ADB). The
     path is MEM/WB.rd -> forward compare (carry chain) -> forward mux
     (3 LUTs) -> alu_a mux -> 33x33 DSP (3.8 ns) -> 4-LUT ALU result
     mux -> BSRAM ADB (paths 6, 15-17). Synthesis cannot know that a
     MUL result never addresses memory.
r1s1 already measured the IPC cost of a 2-stage MUL at only +0.8%
cycles. A cleaner pipeline-control topology costs nothing in cycles.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Restructure the EX-stage datapath and pipeline-control wiring so that
neither path exists any more:
1. Redirect decoupling (A). The IF/ID instruction is raw io_imemData;
   redirect and flush only clear the valid bit. The regfile read
   addresses, decoder, imm_gen and load-use compare do not depend on
   redirect. A load-use stall that a wrong-path instruction falsely
   raises is harmless, because redirect overrides the PC hold and the
   ID/EX kill overrides the hold. Flush/kill clears only ID/EX valid,
   reg_write, mem_read, mem_write, is_branch, is_jump, is_div and
   is_mul, instead of a sync RESET on about 200 ID/EX flops. Redirect
   then fans out only to the PC mux and those few bits.
2. Registered one-hot forwarding selects, computed in ID for the next
   cycle. They compare the incoming rs1/rs2 against ID/EX.rd (the next
   EX/MEM) and EX/MEM.rd (the next MEM/WB). When ID/EX holds (dmem
   stall, ex_busy), they are recomputed against what EX/MEM and MEM/WB
   will hold next cycle, so they stay bit-identical to r1s0's EX-time
   selection. The EX operand mux becomes a registered-select AND-OR,
   with no 5-bit comparator carry chain in front of it.
3. MEM merges the WB write-data mux (mem_to_reg ? load : alu) into one
   MEM/WB.result field. fwd_mem_wb and the regfile write-first bypass
   then come straight from a register.
4. A dedicated AGU adder (forwarded rs1 + imm) computes the dmem
   address in EX and registers it as EX/MEM.mem_addr. That register
   drives io_dmemAddr and the misalign/byte-mask logic, so the BSRAM
   address register sees only forward mux -> adder.
5. The multiplier spans EX->MEM. EX/MEM latches the forwarded rs1/rs2
   values (they already exist for RVFI) and the signedness bits. The
   33x33 DSP product is formed in MEM and selected into MEM/WB.result.
   An instruction in ID that uses the rd of a MUL* in ID/EX gets the
   same 1-bubble interlock as load-use (OR the mul flag into
   hazard_unit's load-use condition). Under RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS the
   ALTOPS MUL stand-ins move with it, computed in MEM from the same
   latched operands.
6. The branch/JAL target pc+imm is precomputed in ID into
   ID/EX.br_target, along with its misalign bit (imm[1] for B/J types,
   since the PC is always word-aligned). EX's redirect path is then
   forward mux -> compare -> redirect.
Expected result: the worst path drops to the EX ALU path (registered
select -> 2-level forward mux -> adder/shifter -> about 3-level result
mux -> EX/MEM), roughly 12-14 ns instead of 22 ns, so Fmax rises from
about 48 MHz to about 65-75 MHz. Cycle count rises by about 1%
(MUL-use bubbles, as in r1s1), for a net gain of about +30-45%
fitness.

title: Zero-bubble BTB (32-entry, 2-bit ctr) with ID-verified targets and a redirect path decoupled from IF/hazard
motivation:
Every taken BRANCH/JAL/JALR resolves in EX and costs exactly ONE bubble
(IF/ID is combinational off the PC register, so only the instruction
at pc+4 that is being decoded under the branch is killed). r1s2's trace
model assumed a 2-cycle penalty, which is why it predicted 13.6% cycle
savings but measured 6.8% (4.49M -> 4.19M timed cycles for 10 CoreMark
iterations, same pipeline shape as r1s0). So a BTB on this pipeline is
worth ~6.5% cycles, and it only wins the tournament (>4.6%) if it
costs ~0 Fmax on top of r1s0.

r1s0's 48.4 MHz critical path is
  ID/EX -> fwd mux -> branch_cond -> redirect -> if_stage NOP mux
        -> hazard load_use (rs1/rs2 compares) -> stall_id/flush_id
        -> ~230 ID/EX flops (sync clear + CE)
i.e. clock_ibuf > u_id > u_ex > u_if > u_hazard > u_id. r1s2 made
redirect a 32-bit (actual_next != pred_next_pc) compare at the end of
that chain, which would have lengthened it. Two observations let a
predictor shorten it instead:
 (a) The NOP-masking of the IF/ID bundle on `redirect` is redundant:
     whenever redirect=1, ID/EX is either flushed (!dmem_stall) or
     held (dmem_stall), never captures, and the PC takes
     redirect_target with priority over stall_if. So load_use can be
     computed from the raw fetched instruction, and the IF->hazard
     segment drops out of the redirect path entirely.
 (b) A bubble only needs its valid + side-effect control bits cleared,
     not all ~230 ID/EX bits, so flush_id's fanout can shrink ~20x.
And the mispredict decision can be made a single LUT level after
branch_cond if the target correctness check is done a stage earlier
(in ID, off any forwarding path), leaving EX to resolve direction only.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
1. Predictor (new rtl/branch_predictor.sv): 32-entry direct-mapped BTB,
   index pc[6:2], tag pc[19:7] (13b, i.e. a full tag over the 1 MB code
   window), target[19:2] (18b), 2-bit counter; data in inferred
   LUT-RAM (async read, sync write), 32 valid bits in reset-cleared
   flops. Lookup from the PC register: hit = valid && tag match;
   pred_taken = hit && ctr[1]; pred_target = {12'b0, target, 2'b00}.
   Only BRANCH and JAL are ever allocated (never JALR: its target
   depends on forwarded rs1 and checking it would sit on the critical
   path; JALR is 0.5% of instrs and keeps today's 1-bubble cost).
   Update port is driven from the EX/MEM REGISTER (one cycle after
   resolve, so no EX combinational logic feeds the LUT-RAM write):
   valid, non-trapping BRANCH/JAL in EX/MEM ->
     taken  : write {tag, branch_target[19:2], hit ? sat_inc(ctr)
              : (JAL ? 2'b11 : 2'b10)}, set valid
     !taken & hit: write same tag/target with sat_dec(ctr)
   (EX/MEM.branch_target = pc+imm is the correct target for both
   BRANCH and JAL.) pred_hit/pred_ctr ride down IF/ID -> ID/EX -> EX/MEM.

2. IF: PC priority reset > redirect > stall > (pred_taken ? pred_target
   : pc+4). pred_* on the IF/ID bundle are forced to 0 when the bundle
   is a bubble (imem stall), and are produced in the same cycle the PC
   advances, so the bit carried with an instruction always matches the
   path actually fetched. out.instr/out.valid are masked ONLY by imem
   stall (no longer by redirect).

3. ID: verify the prediction off the critical path:
     pred_ok = pred_taken && (is_branch || (is_jump && !is_jalr))
               && (pc + imm == pred_target)
   (imem_data in the FPGA bench is an LFSR register, so this is
   reg -> imm_gen -> carry chain -> 32b eq -> ID/EX, well short of the
   EX loop). Register pred_taken, pred_ok, pred_hit, pred_ctr in ID/EX.
   On flush, clear only valid, reg_write, mem_read, mem_write,
   is_branch, is_jump, is_jalr, is_div, pred_taken, pred_ok (data
   fields become don't-care in bubbles: every consumer is gated by
   valid or by one of these bits). Hold (stall) behaviour unchanged.

     redirect        = misalign_fault ? pred_taken
                     : taken ? !pred_ok : pred_taken
     redirect_target = (taken && !misalign_fault) ? existing target
                                                  : pc + 4

   direction only; redirect stays one LUT level after branch_cond, the
   same depth as today's (branch_taken || is_jump) && !misalign.

   architectural next PC), so pc_fwd/pc_bwd checks are unaffected.

   flush_if = imem_stall only. stall_id no longer depends on redirect;

   drives only ~10 control flops.

(~6-6.5% fewer cycles, r1s2's measured number minus JALR and the

the 2x5-bit load_use compares and ~220 sync-clear loads, so Fmax

title: Cut the shared regfile-BSRAM -> operand prefix to 1 LUT (no reset/bypass fixups, pre-muxed forward sources) and flatten the ALU-result and branch-condition tails
motivation:
I ran `make timing TARGET=bench` on the champion (r2s1, 65.3 MHz at
place_option 0). The regfile is mapped to two BSRAM SDPBs
(cpu/u_rf/regs_regs_0_0_s / _s0). The read address comes from the
imem word (lfsr -> ADB), so the ID/EX rs?_val register is the BSRAM read
register and the read data (tC2Q 2.26 ns) appears in EX. Both near-tied
worst paths start at that BSRAM DO and share the same prefix:
  path 1 (-10.315 ns, 14 cells): DO -> 2 LUTs in u_id
    (id_ex_w.rs1_val_*_s15/_s14: Gowin's fixups for the reg_file
    reset loop, emulated with a side LUT-RAM regs_ER_RS, plus the
    write-first bypass and x0 handling) -> 2 LUTs forward mux
    (u_ex/rs1_*_s2, _s0) -> alu_a AUIPC mux -> 2 LUTs in u_alu ->
    6 LUT chain of result muxing (n692/n700/n684_s9/_s5/_s1/_s0:
    5-bit op case + is_jump/is_div select) -> EX/MEM.alu_result.
  paths 7-25 (-10.25 ns): DO -> 1 LUT in u_id -> 3 LUT forward mux
    (u_ex/rs2_*_s2/_s1/_s0) -> compare carry chain -> 2+ LUTs
    branch_cond/redirect -> PC CE/D and ID/EX kill_q RESET.
So 4 of the ~14 levels on both twin paths are operand fixups after the
BSRAM. Every other input to them (EX/MEM.alu_result, MEM/WB.result,
imm, pc) is a plain register that is ready about 2 ns before DO. As the
r2s0/r2s1 lessons show, breaking only one twin gains nothing. The fix
must shorten the shared prefix, and it must not change CPI.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
A pure circuit restructure with the same pipeline, the same latencies
and an identical cycle count:
1. reg_file: delete the synchronous reset loop (the source of the
   regs_ER_RS emulation LUT-RAM and its output mux). Zero-fill it with an
   `initial` block instead, which gives the BSRAM power-up init and zero
   init in Verilator and formal. Also delete the write-first bypass and
   the rs==0 muxes, so the read is just regs[addr] and BSRAM DO is the
   operand source with no Gowin-inserted fixup logic.
2. The bypass becomes a forward source. Add a "last write" register
   wl_q <= w_data whenever w_en (in core.sv). In ID, forward_unit also
   computes fwd_rs?_wl = w_en && w_addr == rs? (priority below EX/MEM
   and MEM/WB) and zero_rs? = (rs? == 0). From these, ID registers a
   sel_ram_rs? = !(ex|wb|wl|zero). All of these are held with ID/EX on
   stall_id, as today. wl_q is stable across dmem stalls because
   MEM/WB.valid = 0 then.
3. EX operand = one LUT after DO. other_rs? = AND-OR of
   {EX/MEM.alu_result, MEM/WB.result, wl_q} under the registered
   one-hot selects (0 for x0). It is built only from registers, in
   parallel with the BSRAM clock-to-out. Then
   rs? = sel_ram_rs? ? DO : other_rs?, which feeds the AGU, the branch
   compare, store data, and the MUL/div operands. The ALU B operand gets
   its own copy, opb = sel_ram_b ? DO2 : other_b, where other_b also
   includes imm (sel_ram_b = sel_ram_rs2 && !alu_src). This takes the
   alu_src mux off the DO path.
4. Fold AUIPC into ID: the existing ID pc+imm adder (br_target) is
   latched into ID/EX.imm for AUIPC, and the op becomes ALU_LUI (out = b).
   alu_a is then always rs1, which removes the alu_a_* LUT.
5. ALU result as a one-hot AND-OR: ID decodes registered one-hot group
   selects {addsub, sll, srl/sra, slt/sltu, logic(and/or/xor/lui),
   link, div} plus sub/arith/unsigned flags. EX uses one shared adder
   a + (b ^ {32{sub}}) + sub (SLT/SLTU from its carry and sign bits),
   separate SLL and SRL/SRA shifters, and a logic group. ID precomputes
   link = pc+4. EX/MEM.alu_result's D input is a single OR of the
   gated groups, with the adder and shifters at the last level. This
   replaces the 5-bit case decode and the is_jump/is_div priority mux
   (the 6-LUT n684 chain).
6. Branch-condition tail: ID registers a one-hot condition select
   (eq, ne, lt, ge) plus an unsigned bit, and is_branch_ok =
   is_branch && !br_misalign. EX computes eq (XOR-reduce) and one
   33-bit lt carry chain (signed/unsigned via the registered extend
   bit), so redirect = is_jump | is_branch_ok & cond is one LUT after
   the chain. branch_trap stays off the redirect path.
Expected: both twin paths lose about 3 LUT levels in the prefix (4 to 1)
plus 1 to 3 in their tails. That cuts about 3-4 ns from the 15.3 ns
data delay, so Fmax goes from 65 to about 76-82 MHz until the next path
(dmem load align -> MEM/WB.result, or the decode/hazard -> PC CE path)
limits it. With an unchanged cycle count, that is about +15 to +25%
fitness. Implementers should re-run `make timing`. If Gowin still
inserts a read-during-write collision LUT after DO, it is semantically
redundant (sel_wl overrides that case), so check the .tr path and keep
the RTL read port a bare registered regs[addr].

lesson: - 2026-10-01 hyp-20261001-001-r3s0 (improvement, +36.76%): Any regfile semantics on the RAM read port (a synchronous reset loop, which Gowin emulates with a side LUT-RAM plus an output mux, the write-first bypass, and the rs==0 muxes) turn into LUT levels after the BSRAM DO, which arrives about 2 ns after every other register, and so they sat on the shared prefix of both twin critical paths; making the read a bare registered regs[addr] (zero-filled with an `initial` block), handling the bypass as a "last write" wl_q forward source, and choosing all non-RAM sources in ID with registered one-hot selects AND-ORed from registers only leaves one 2:1 LUT after DO, and together with one-hot AND-OR ALU-result and branch-condition tails this gave about twice the predicted +18% at unchanged CPI, so keep late-arriving hard-block outputs at most one LUT from their consumer and do all other selection in parallel from registers.

title: Classic 5-stage: IF/ID register + explicit sync-read regfile so the BSRAM read leaves EX; ID-stage JAL/BTFN redirect
motivation:
`make timing` on the r2s1 champion (65.3 MHz, place_option 0) shows all
of the top 25 setup paths starting at the regfile, which Gowin placed in
BSRAM (regs_regs_0_0_s at BSRAM_R10[4]; 6 BSRAM = 4 dmem + 2 regfile
copies). Gowin uses ID/EX.rs?_val as the BSRAM's synchronous read
register (the address latched is the fetched word's rs field), so the
read itself runs in the EX cycle. Path 1 (15.28 ns data, 14 levels):
  BSRAM CLKB->DO tC2Q 2.26 ns + route 1.20 ns
  -> id_ex_w.rs1_val_s15/s14 (2 LUTs: read-during-write / WB bypass)
  -> u_ex rs1_s2/s0 (forward mux, 2 LUTs) -> alu_a -> u_alu (2)
  -> n692/n700/n684 x4 (result mux) -> EX/MEM.alu_result.
Paths 7-25 have the same front end and end at pc CE and kill_q RESET
(branch_cond -> redirect). About 5 ns of every critical path (BSRAM
clock-to-out + route + 2 bypass LUTs) is the regfile read, and it
cannot leave EX: the read address is only known after the word is
fetched, so the read takes a cycle and that cycle is EX. In the timed
netlist io_imemData is a register (the LFSR in fpga/core_bench_si.sv),
so an IF/ID register costs no IF-side timing. LESSONS r2s1 called this
regfile LUT-RAM; the report shows BSRAM.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Make the pipeline a classic 5-stage IF -> ID -> EX -> MEM -> WB, and do
the regfile read in its own (ID) cycle.
1. IF/ID register {pc, instr, valid} in if_stage, captured when not
   held. A bubble (valid=0) is loaded on imem stall, on EX redirect and
   on ID redirect. It is held on load-use, dmem stall and ex_busy.
   Decoder, imm_gen, forward_unit and the load-use compare all read
   these flops.
2. Explicit synchronous-read regfile (rewrite reg_file.sv): two read
   ports, read address = the NEXT IF/ID rs fields
   (hold ? IF/ID.instr[rs] : imem_data[rs]). The data out is valid in
   ID. Re-reading the held address every cycle keeps a held operand
   from going stale under multi-cycle holds (div, dmem stall). Two
   bypasses run in ID, both with select logic from registers:
     (a) collision: a write at the same edge the address is latched.
         Register (w_en && w_addr == raddr) and w_data, and select them.
     (b) write-first: the MEM/WB instruction writing during the ID
         cycle. Compare IF/ID rs with MEM/WB.rd (valid && reg_write)
         and select MEM/WB.result.
   ID/EX.rs?_val then becomes a real flop with logic in front of it, so
   Gowin can no longer absorb it as the BSRAM read register. The BSRAM
   tC2Q, its route and the bypass LUTs move into ID: about 2.3+1.2+2x0.9
   = 5.3 ns, a short stage. Forwarding distances are unchanged:
   EX/MEM (d=1) and MEM/WB (d=2) are forwarded in EX, d=3 uses bypass
   (b) and d=4 uses bypass (a).
3. EX now starts at real flops: ID/EX -> fwd mux -> alu_a/b -> ALU ->
   result mux -> EX/MEM. About 10 levels, roughly 11 ns, instead of
   15.3 ns, so Fmax goes from 65 to about 85 MHz. The branch ->
   redirect -> PC CE/kill paths lose the same ~4-5 ns front end.
4. The extra stage adds 1 bubble to EX-resolved redirects. Win most of
   it back in ID, from flops only:
   - JAL (already pc+imm in ID, with misaligned JAL turned into a trap)
     redirects from ID.
   - BTFN: a BRANCH with imm[31]=1 and imm[1]=0 is predicted taken and
     redirects from ID to pc+imm.
   - The ID redirect fires only when the IF/ID instruction actually
     moves into ID/EX (valid, not held, no load-use, no EX redirect).
     It kills only the word being fetched (1 bubble, the same as a
     taken branch today).
   - ID/EX gets pred_taken and alt_target, where
     alt_target = pred_taken ? pc+4 : br_target, precomputed in ID.
     EX redirects when (is_branch && (cond ^ pred_taken)) or for JALR.
     The EX redirect target is is_jalr ? agu : alt_target, so no new
     mux level. JAL never redirects in EX.
   - EX redirect has priority in the PC mux and kills IF/ID and ID/EX.
   - pc_next/RVFI still report the real next PC. The misaligned-branch
     trap logic is unchanged (a misaligned target is never predicted).
CPI model from r1s2's measured stats (2.94M insns, CPI 1.54;
BRANCH 18.1%, taken 10.1%, JAL 1.7%, JALR 0.5%, 1-bubble redirects
today = 0.123 CPI): with ID JAL and BTFN, about 0.19 CPI of redirect
bubbles, i.e. +0.066 CPI (about -4% IPC). Without BTFN it would be
-6.4%. Fmax +25-30% x IPC 0.96 gives about +20% fitness.
Keep all r2s1 timing structure: registered one-hot forward selects,
register-sourced MEM/WB.result bypass, the AGU for io_dmemAddr, the
EX->MEM DSP MUL behind the 1-bubble interlock, the iterative divider
with registered ex_busy, and narrow ID/EX kill.

title: Same-cycle predecode branch prediction: 128-entry bimodal BHT + IF-side B/J target adder, no BTB
motivation:
On r2s1 (the champion, 65.1 MHz, 4.53M timed cycles) every taken BRANCH,
JAL and JALR resolves in EX and costs one bubble. IF/ID is
combinational off the PC register, so the bubble is the pc+4 word that
gets killed. From the baseline trace (r1s2), taken branches are 10.1%
of retired instructions, JAL 1.7% and JALR 0.5%, about 360k redirects
per run. r2s2 measured what removing them is worth: a 32-entry BTB cut
r1s0's cycles by 6.4% (4.49M -> 4.20M). That gain did not reach the
score because Fmax stayed at r1s0's 48 MHz, and LESSONS says to re-apply
it on r2s1 off the regfile -> ALU -> EX/MEM critical path.
A BTB is not needed on this pipeline. Two facts allow a cheaper design
that is likely more accurate:
 (1) IF and ID are the same cycle. The fetched word is decoded in the
     cycle its PC is in the PC register, so the next-PC choice can use
     the real opcode and immediate of the instruction being fetched.
     Stored targets, tags and the ID-side "is this really a branch with
     this target" check (r2s2) are not needed.
 (2) In the timed netlist (fpga/core_bench_si.sv), io_imemData is an
     LFSR flop and io_imemAddr feeds only the LED XOR. So "imem data ->
     small immediate mux -> 32-bit adder -> PC mux -> PC flop" starts
     at a flop's clock-to-out. That is about 1 LUT + a carry chain + 2
     LUTs, far shorter than the 20.6 ns / 14-level regfile -> ALU path
     that sets Fmax. The adder already exists: ID computes
     br_target = pc + imm for ID/EX.
With the target computed from the instruction itself, JAL is always
predicted correctly, including the first time it is seen. A branch is
wrong only when the direction predictor is wrong. There are no
capacity or alias misses on targets, and a stale entry cannot point a
non-branch somewhere else.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Make branch/JAL prediction a same-cycle IF/ID decision. EX only fixes
mispredicts.

1. New rtl/branch_predictor.sv: a bimodal BHT with 128 x 2-bit
   saturating counters, indexed by pc[8:2]. Use flops with synchronous
   reset to 2'b01 (weakly not-taken) so sim and formal never see X.
   LUT-RAM is allowed only if it stays X-free in every simulator used.
   - Read port: async, indexed by the PC register (IF). It is a
     flop-sourced 128:1 mux, ready in parallel with the instruction
     decode. Output ctr[1:0].
   - Write port: indexed by EX/MEM.pc[8:2]. It is written when EX/MEM
     holds a valid, non-trapping BRANCH and MEM/WB is advancing
     (!hold_mem_wb), so each dynamic branch updates exactly once.
     Data = sat_inc/sat_dec of the counter snapshot taken at predict
     time (carried down the pipe), using the registered taken bit.
     Updating from EX/MEM (one cycle late) keeps branch_cond off the
     predictor-write timing path.

2. if_stage.sv: fetch-side predecode and target.
   - fetch_is_br  = opcode==7'b1100011 && funct3 not in {2,3}
     (exactly the decoder's legal set).
     fetch_is_jal = opcode==7'b1101111.
   - A dedicated fetch adder: fetch_tgt = pc + (instr[3] ? J-imm : B-imm).
     The immediate select is a 1-LUT mux on raw instr bits; do not go
     through the full imm_gen case.
   - pred_taken = (fetch_is_jal && !Jimm[1]) ||
     (fetch_is_br && bht_ctr[1] && !Bimm[1]).
     A misaligned target is never predicted, so the trap behaviour is
     unchanged.
   - PC next-state, with redirect as the LAST mux level so the EX
     redirect path gains no depth:
       pc_seq = stall ? pc : (pred_taken ? fetch_tgt : pc + 4);
       pc_d   = reset ? 0 : redirect ? redirect_target : pc_seq;
   - Export pred_taken, bht_ctr, fetch_tgt and pc+4 in the IF/ID bundle.

3. id_stage.sv / core_pkg.sv: carry the prediction.
   - ID/EX gets these new fields: pred_taken; bht_ctr[1:0]; pc_plus4
     (registered, so EX needs no pc+4 adder); and
     alt_target = pred_taken ? pc_plus4 : fetch_tgt, the address to
     redirect to if the prediction is wrong.
   - ID/EX.br_target can come from fetch_tgt, since it is only used for
     BRANCH/JAL.
   - pred_taken MUST join the kill_q side-effect bits (cleared on
     reset/flush, AND-ed with in.valid). Otherwise a bubble that
     carries pred_taken=1 would redirect.
   - EX/MEM gets: bht_ctr, br_taken (actual direction) and the
     BRANCH-valid bit, all for the BHT update.

4. ex_stage.sv: redirect only on a misprediction.
   - actual_taken = branch_taken (cond && !br_misalign) || is_jump.
   - redirect = (actual_taken != pred_taken) || is_jalr.
     It is a single LUT after branch_cond, because pred_taken is a
     registered bit. Do it generically so that if formal ever gets a
     predicted non-CF instruction, it redirects to pc+4.
   - redirect_target = is_jalr ? (jalr_misalign ? pc_plus4 : {agu[31:1],0})
                                : alt_target.
     The select uses only registered bits. Nothing in the target mux
     depends on the branch compare any more.
   - EX/MEM.pc_next (RVFI-only) stays the architectural next PC,
     computed exactly as today (taken/jump ? target : pc+4). The
     JAL/JALR link value uses the registered pc_plus4.
   - A JAL now never redirects. A JALR always redirects, as before:
     it is only 0.5% of instructions and its target needs rs1.

5. hazard_unit / forward_unit are unchanged. When a valid
   instruction is captured into ID/EX, stall_if is always 0 and
   redirect is 0, so the PC really followed the prediction stored in
   ID/EX.pred_taken. During a load-use / dmem / div stall, the PC holds
   and the word is refetched and re-predicted. An EX redirect has
   priority over a same-cycle IF prediction, and flush_id kills the
   predicted instruction.

Expected effect: bubbles drop from about 360k taken redirects to about
50-60k (bimodal mispredicts, about 10% of 532k branches, plus 15k
JALR). Measured against r2s2's BTB result, that should cut cycles by
6-7% (to about 4.22M). Fmax should stay about 65 MHz. The new IF
path is flop -> 1 LUT -> 32-bit carry -> 2 LUT -> PC. The EX redirect
path and the regfile -> ALU -> EX/MEM.alu_result critical path keep
their depth. EX loses its pc+4 adder and target mux logic. Cost is
about +300 LUT and about +270 FF.

changes.description: New module: 128-entry x 2-bit bimodal BHT (flops, sync reset to 2'b01). Async read indexed by IF pc[8:2]. One write port, indexed by EX/MEM.pc[8:2], with saturating update from the carried counter snapshot and the registered taken bit.

Raw-instruction predecode (legal BRANCH / JAL only) and a dedicated pc + (instr[3] ? Jimm : Bimm) fetch adder. pred_taken = JAL, or BRANCH with BHT ctr[1], target aligned. Next PC = redirect ? redirect_target : (stall ? pc : pred_taken ? fetch_tgt : pc+4), with redirect as the last mux level. Export pred_taken, bht_ctr, fetch_tgt and pc+4 in the IF/ID bundle.

title: Make the branch condition the last mux select (PC / ID-EX kill / no EX-MEM ctrl dependence) and flatten the shifter -> alu_result tail
motivation:
`make timing` on r3s0 (place_option 0, 79.3 MHz, 12.58 ns data path) shows
25 worst paths all starting at the regfile BSRAM DO and within 0.21 ns of each
other, in two groups (break both or nothing moves, per the r2s0 lesson):

A) Branch cone (paths 1-4, 7-25): DO 7.59 -> rs2 2:1 mux 9.43 -> 33-cell
   compare carry chain 12.04 -> net 1.4 -> redirect_Z_s1 -> redirect_Z_s0 ->
   redirect_Z_s (fanout 34) 15.40, then
     * u_if/pc_30_s3 (fanout 30) -> pc_*_s1/CE        17.88
     * u_id/n944_s0 (fanout 9)   -> kill_q_*/RESET    17.80
     * 3 more LUTs (n1326_s4/s3/s2) -> EX/MEM ctrl.reg_write/D 17.905
   So 3 LUT levels + two high-fanout nets sit between the compare and every
   consumer. The reg_write endpoint exists only because ctrl_with_trap clears
   reg_write/mem_read/mem_write on branch_trap, but a BRANCH never has those bits
   set (decoder), so that clear is dead logic that synthesis cannot remove
   (the bits are separate ID/EX flops). branch_trap only matters for is_illegal,
   which is RVFI-only and pruned.
B) Shifter cone (paths 5, 6, 10): DO -> rs1 2:1 mux 9.00 (fanout 16, then a
   3.38 ns net) -> u_alu n57_s4 -> n57_s2 -> n1203_s13 -> n1203_s6 ->
   n1219_s3 -> n1219_s0 -> EX/MEM alu_result/D 17.80: six LUT levels from
   the shifter through the per-bit result OR, which also ORs in link and
   div_result.

B) Shifter cone (paths 5, 6, 10): DO -> rs1 2:1 mux 9.00 (fanout 16, then a

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Same CPI and same pipeline; only the logic after the EX operand muxes changes.

A) Branch / redirect:
 1. ctrl_with_trap clears reg_write / mem_read / mem_write only on
    (mem_misalign | jalr_misalign). Both use only agu_sum[1:0] plus registered
    bits. branch_trap is ORed into is_illegal alone. EX/MEM.ctrl then has no
    dependence on the compare chain.
 2. ID registers a 3-bit condition code that already includes br_ok:
    br_ok_q, br_use_lt_q (BLT/BGE/BLTU/BGEU), br_inv_q (BNE/BGE/BGEU). EX
    computes ONE late signal:
       take = br_ok_q & ((br_use_lt_q ? lt : eq) ^ br_inv_q)   (one LUT5)
    eq = XOR-reduce, lt = the existing 33-bit chain.
 3. Every redirect consumer uses `take` only as the last 2:1 select. Every
    other input is precomputed from registers or the AGU chain, in parallel:
      - PC: pc_d = take ? br_target_q : pc_nt, where
        pc_nt = is_jump_q ? jump_tgt : (stall_if ? pc : pc + 4) and
        jump_tgt = !is_jalr ? br_target_q
                   : (jalr_misalign ? link : {agu_sum[31:1],1'b0}).
        Write it as a plain D mux (no clock-enable or priority chain behind
        `take`).
      - ID/EX kill_q: kill_d[k] = kill_nt[k] & ~(take & ~dmem_stall). kill_nt
        is the existing reset / load_use / jump / stall / capture logic
        without the branch term. This is a D-input AND instead of the
        synchronous RESET pin driven by the redirect OR.
      - EX/MEM.pc_next (RVFI only) may keep using the full redirect.
    `redirect` (is_jump_q | take) stays as a wire for any remaining user.
    Compute `take` twice with /* synthesis syn_keep=1 */, once for the 32 PC
    bits and once for kill_q, so each high-fanout net is short.
 Expected: chain end -> PC/kill_q D goes from 3 LUTs + 2 high-fanout nets to
 1 LUT5 + 1 net + 1 LUT3, about -1.5 to -2 ns. The reg_write endpoint drops
 out of the top list.

B) ALU result tail:
 1. Pre-merge the register-sourced result groups in EX into one early term,
    early = ({32{alu_link}} & link) | ({32{alu_div}} & div_result), which is
    settled well before DO arrives. Pass it into alu as one input.
 2. Logic group as one LUT5 per bit: ID registers a 2-bit logic op
    (00 AND, 01 OR, 10 XOR, 11 pass-b for LUI/AUIPC) plus a logic enable,
    replacing four separate gated terms.
 3. Fold each shifter's group select into its last mux stage
    (sll_g[i] = sel_sll & (shamt[4] ? s[i-16] : s[i]); likewise for sr with
    sign fill). The per-bit tail is then one OR of
    {add_g, sll_g, sr_g, logic_g, early}, and SLT folds into bit 0.
 4. Give the shifters their own copy of the rs1 DO 2:1 mux (syn_keep), so the
    rs1 net with fanout 16 (3.38 ns) no longer feeds the shifter. The
    adder / AGU / branch compare / EX-MEM rs1_val keep the existing copy.
 Target: at most 4 LUT levels from the rs1 mux to alu_result D, which saves
 about 1.5 ns.

Both groups must be done for Fmax to move. The next tier (DO -> adder chain
-> 1-level tail, and DO -> AGU -> mem_addr) is estimated at about 14 ns
arrival vs 17.9 ns now. Expected Fmax: about 79 -> 88 MHz on p0 and 89 ->
about 98 MHz median, roughly +10% fitness with unchanged cycles.

changes.description: ctrl_with_trap: kill reg_write/mem_read/mem_write only on mem_misalign|jalr_misalign; is_illegal |= branch_trap. Compute take = br_ok_q & ((use_lt ? lt : eq) ^ inv) (two syn_keep copies), export take + jump_q + precomputed jump_tgt; build early = link|div term and pass to alu; duplicate the rs1 DO 2:1 mux for the shifters (syn_keep).
PC next-state as a plain D mux: pc_d = take ? br_target : (is_jump ? jump_tgt : (stall ? pc : pc+4)), take as the last select; no CE/priority chain behind the branch condition.

Register br_ok/br_use_lt/br_inv (replacing br_eq/ne/lt/ge one-hots), 2-bit logic op + logic enable; kill_q next-state = kill_nt & ~(take & ~dmem_stall) as a D-input term instead of a sync reset driven by redirect; export br_target/link/is_jump for the IF PC mux.
flush_id no longer includes redirect (the branch-taken kill is applied in id_stage as the last D-term); jump kill (is_jump_q, registered) and load_use stay in flush.

Logic group as LUT5 (2-bit op + enable); fold sll/sr group selects into the last shifter stage; add `early` input; output = add_g | slt(bit0) | sll_g | sr_g | logic_g | early. mul_unit (ALTOPS and real arms) unchanged.
id_ex_t: replace br_eq/br_ne/br_lt/br_ge with br_use_lt/br_inv (br_ok kept), replace alu_and/alu_or/alu_xor/alu_lui with alu_logic + alu_lop[1:0].
Wire take / jump_q / jump_tgt / br_target from EX to IF, take + dmem_stall to id_stage kill logic; drop redirect from hazard flush.
Update RV32I ALU vectors to the new logic-op encoding and early input; keep the exact-result MUL* vectors on mul_unit unchanged.

ctrl_with_trap: kill reg_write/mem_read/mem_write only on mem_misalign|jalr_misalign; is_illegal |= branch_trap. lesson: - 2026-10-01 hyp-20261001-001-r4s0 (improvement, +10.04%): On r3s0 the two twin cones from the BSRAM DO (branch compare -> 3 LUTs and two high-fanout redirect nets -> PC CE / ID-EX kill RESET / EX-MEM reg_write, and the fanout-16 rs1 mux -> shifter -> 6-level ALU-result OR) were within 0.21 ns of each other, and fixing both at once gave the predicted +10% at unchanged CPI: the fixes were making a late signal (`take`) only the last 2:1 select of a plain D-input mux (not a clock-enable, sync reset or priority chain), cutting false dependences that synthesis cannot prune across separate flops (the dead branch_trap clear of reg_write/mem_*), duplicating high-fanout operand muxes with syn_keep, and pre-merging register-sourced result groups so the per-bit tail is one OR of pre-gated groups; so audit every late-signal endpoint for CE/SR pins and dead control terms, not just its LUT depth.

title: Take the regfile BSRAM DO out of EX: IF/ID register + ID-cycle sync regfile read on r3s0's flat EX, with ID-stage JAL/BTFN redirects
motivation:
r3s0 (champion, 89.05 MHz median, seeds 79.3/89.05/89.05, 4,527,646
cycles) is limited by an EX path that starts at the regfile BSRAM:
cpu/u_rf/regs_regs_0_0_s0 (DO, tC2Q ~2.3 ns plus a long BSRAM route)
-> 1 operand LUT -> 33-bit compare/add carry chain -> branch_cond /
trap -> EX/MEM.ctrl.reg_write (11 levels). Its twins (ALU -> EX/MEM.alu_result,
redirect -> PC/kill) share the same DO prefix. r3s0 already
trimmed everything after DO to one LUT, so what remains is the DO
itself: ~3 ns of a 11.2 ns period is hard-block clock-to-out plus
routing, which no further micro-opt can remove while ID/EX.rs?_val
is the BSRAM read register.
r3s1 already tested the structural fix on the older r2s1 base: an
IF/ID register, a sync-read regfile in ID, and ID-stage JAL/BTFN
redirects. It cost only +2.8% cycles (4,653,306 vs 4,527,646). Its
EX stage was still r2s1's (5-bit case result mux, 2-3 LUT forward
mux), and it still reached 80.8 MHz median (90.0 MHz on one seed).
It was never combined with r3s0's flat EX (one-hot AND-OR ALU tail,
one-hot branch condition, registered selects). The combination
should beat either one alone. LESSONS r3s1 asks for exactly this
check: is the ~3 ns still left to move worth ~3-4% CPI? At an
11.2 ns period it is (~25% of the cycle).

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Make the pipeline IF -> ID -> EX -> MEM -> WB with real IF/ID flops.
The regfile is read synchronously in ID, so ID/EX.rs?_val becomes a
plain fabric flop and EX starts from registers only. Keep all of
r3s0's EX structure.
1. IF/ID register {pc, instr, valid} (if_stage). Load a bubble on
   imem stall, on EX redirect and on ID redirect. Hold it on
   load-use, dmem stall and ex_busy. Decoder, imm_gen, forward_unit
   and the load-use compare all read these flops, which takes the
   imem DO -> decode -> load-use -> PC-CE path off the period.
2. Sync-read regfile (reg_file.sv): bare regs[raddr_q] with the
   `initial` zero fill. The read address is the NEXT IF/ID rs field:
   hold ? IF/ID.instr[rs] : io_imemData[rs]. Re-reading the held
   address every cycle keeps a held operand fresh across div and
   dmem holds. ID builds ID/EX.rs?_val = one 2:1 LUT after DO, with
   selects computed from flops in parallel with the BSRAM read:
     (a) collision (write at the edge the address was latched): a
         registered (w_en && w_addr == raddr) flag picks wl_q;
     (b) write-during-ID (MEM/WB writing this cycle): IF/ID.rs ==
         MEM/WB.rd && reg_write && valid picks MEM/WB.result.
   The bypass AND-OR of (a)/(b) uses registers only, as in r3s0.
   Also latch a separate ID/EX.b_val that is imm when alu_src, else
   the same rs2 value. The imm/rs2 choice then leaves EX entirely.
3. EX operands come only from registers. Each operand is
   {EX/MEM.alu_result (d=1), MEM/WB.result (d=2), ID/EX.rs?_val/b_val}
   under registered one-hot selects computed in ID (forward_unit
   compares IF/ID.rs against ID/EX.rd and EX/MEM.rd). That is a
   5-input mux, one LUT4+MUX2_LUT5, starting at a flop clk-to-q
   (~0.4 ns) instead of BSRAM DO (~2.3 ns + route). Keep r3s0's
   one-hot ALU tail, shared add/sub, one-hot branch condition, the
   dedicated AGU, the MUL EX->MEM DSP with its 1-bubble interlock, the
   iterative divider with registered ex_busy, and narrow ID/EX kill.
4. Shorten the current worst endpoint: branch_trap only needs to set
   is_illegal (RVFI-only, pruned). BRANCH never has
   reg_write/mem_read/mem_write, so clear those three only on
   mem_misalign | jalr_misalign (AGU low bits). EX/MEM.ctrl.reg_write
   is then no longer behind the full compare chain.
5. Win back most of the extra redirect bubble in ID, from IF/ID
   flops only (as in r3s1). JAL redirects from ID to the existing
   pc+imm (br_target), and a misaligned JAL is still a non-jump
   trap. BTFN: a BRANCH with imm[31]=1 and imm[1]=0 predicts taken
   and redirects from ID. The ID redirect fires only when the IF/ID
   instruction moves into ID/EX (valid, not held, no load-use). EX
   redirect has priority as the last PC-mux level and kills IF/ID +
   ID/EX. ID/EX carries pred_taken and alt_target = pred_taken ?
   pc+4 : br_target, so EX redirects on is_branch && (cond ^
   pred_taken) or JALR, with target is_jalr ? agu : alt_target (no
   new mux level). pc_next/RVFI still report the real next PC.
Expected: EX loses about 2-3 ns (DO clk-to-out and route) and the
branch_trap tail. The ID/IF paths become short (flop-sourced). The
next limiters are probably the EX/MEM -> DSP MUL -> MEM/WB.result
path and redirect -> PC -> imem ADB, both estimated at 8.5-9.5 ns.
So Fmax goes from 89 to about 105-115 MHz. Cycles +2.5-3% (r3s1's
measured CPI cost of the same front end). Fitness about +12 to +22%.

lesson: - 2026-10-01 hyp-20261001-002-r4s1 (regression, +3.64%): Putting r3s1's IF/ID register, ID-cycle sync regfile read and JAL/BTFN ID redirects on r3s0's flat EX gave +3.64% instead of the predicted +15%; since fitness = Fmax*1e7/cycles, at r3s1's ~+2.8% cycles this implies about 95 MHz, not 105-115, and below r4s0's 98 MHz at unchanged CPI with the same branch_trap fix, because once a late BSRAM DO is only one LUT from its consumer, an extra stage does not win back its ~3 ns: the next paths are nearly as long, likely including ones the new stage adds into hard-block inputs (the hold-muxed next-rs read address into the regfile ADB, ID redirect -> PC -> imem ADB); so estimate a stage split's gain from the next-worst path, counting the paths it creates, not from the delay it removes, and do the zero-CPI micro-opts first.

title: Port same-cycle IF predecode + 128x2b bimodal BHT onto r3s0, with redirect/fetch paths kept off the BSRAM-DO critical chain
motivation:
The champion r3s0 (89.05 MHz, 4,527,646 timed cycles) still resolves every
taken BRANCH, JAL and JALR in EX. IF and ID share a cycle (no IF/ID flop),
so each taken control transfer costs exactly one bubble: about 360k
bubbles per run (taken branches ~10.1% of retired instructions, JAL 1.7%,
JALR 0.5%). r3s2 measured the fix on r2s1: same-cycle predecode of the
fetched word + a dedicated pc+imm fetch adder + a 128x2-bit bimodal BHT
cut cycles from 4,527,646 to 4,238,604 (-6.38%) and did NOT lower Fmax
(65.1 -> 68.5 MHz), because io_imemData is a flop in the timed netlist,
so the fetch-target path starts at a flop's clock-to-out instead of at
the late regfile BSRAM DO. r3s2 lost only to r3s0's timing fix; LESSONS
says its CPI gain is independent of that fix and should be ported next.
The cycle count of r3s0 is identical to r2s1 (4,527,646), so the r3s2
saving carries over 1:1: 196.68 * 4527646/4238604 = ~210 (+6.8%) at
unchanged Fmax.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Re-implement r3s2's predictor on top of r3s0 (do not copy r3s2's RTL —
r3s0 restructured ID/EX: one-hot selects, wl_val, br_ok kill bit,
AUIPC folded into ID, link = pc+4 registered).

1. rtl/branch_predictor.sv (new): 128 x 2-bit saturating counters,
   indexed by pc[8:2]. Flops, synchronous reset to 2'b01 (weakly
   not-taken), so Verilator/formal never see X. Async read from the PC
   register (IF). One write port indexed by EX/MEM.pc[8:2], enabled when
   EX/MEM holds a valid, non-trapping BRANCH and MEM/WB advances
   (!hold_mem_wb), data = sat_inc/sat_dec of the counter snapshot that
   was carried down the pipe, using the registered taken bit. Updating
   one cycle late keeps branch_cond off any predictor write path.

2. rtl/if_stage.sv: raw-word predecode and target.
   fetch_is_br  = opcode==1100011 && funct3 not in {2,3} (decoder's legal
   set), fetch_is_jal = opcode==1101111.
   fetch_tgt = pc + (instr[3] ? J-imm : B-imm), a dedicated adder whose
   immediate is a 1-LUT mux on raw instr bits (not through imm_gen).
   pred_taken = (fetch_is_jal && !Jimm[1]) || (fetch_is_br && ctr[1] && !Bimm[1])
   (misaligned targets are never predicted, so trap behaviour is unchanged).
   PC next-state with the EX redirect as the LAST mux level, so the
   DO -> compare chain -> redirect -> PC path gains no depth:
     pc_seq = stall ? pc : (pred_taken ? fetch_tgt : pc + 4);
     pc_d   = reset ? 0 : redirect ? redirect_target : pc_seq;
   Export pred_taken, ctr and fetch_tgt in if_id_t.

3. rtl/id_stage.sv / core_pkg.sv: ID/EX gets pred_taken (as a kill_q
   side-effect bit: AND-ed with in.valid, cleared on reset/flush, so a
   bubble can never redirect), bht_ctr[1:0], and
   alt_target = pred_taken ? pc+4 : fetch_tgt (the mispredict-recovery
   address). br_target / br_misalign for BRANCH/JAL may come from
   fetch_tgt; the existing ID pc+imm adder stays for AUIPC only. Every
   new field is held on stall_id exactly like the existing selects.
   EX/MEM gets bht_ctr, br_taken and a branch-update-valid bit.

4. rtl/ex_stage.sv: redirect only on a misprediction, with NO extra
   LUT after the compare chain. Measured `make timing` on r3s0
   (place_option 0, 79.3 MHz): the top 4 paths are within 0.1 ns —
   BSRAM DO -> 1 LUT -> 33-bit compare -> {EX/MEM.ctrl.reg_write
   (branch_trap), u_if/pc (redirect), u_id/kill_q (flush_id)} at
   17.80-17.91 ns, plus DO -> ALU -> EX/MEM.alu_result at 17.80 ns. So
   a naive (cond ^ pred) XOR would land directly on three of the four
   twins. Instead fold pred_taken into the registered selects in ID:
     ID registers  mp_eq = pred ? br_ne : br_eq,  mp_ne = pred ? br_eq : br_ne,
                   mp_lt = pred ? br_ge : br_lt,  mp_ge = pred ? br_lt : br_ge
     (= the condition under which the branch was MISpredicted), and a
     kill_q bit  redir_const = is_jalr | (is_jump & !pred)
                             | (pred & !is_branch & !is_jump)   (the last
     term never fires for a valid word; it keeps formal safe).
     EX: br_mp   = br_ok & ((mp_eq & eq_v) | (mp_ne & ~eq_v)
                          | (mp_lt & lt_v) | (mp_ge & ~lt_v))
         redirect = redir_const | br_mp
   This is the exact same LUT shape as r3s0's
   `is_jump | br_ok & cond`, so the redirect -> PC and flush_id ->
   kill_q twins keep their depth. redirect_target =
   is_jalr ? (jalr_misalign ? link : {agu[31:1],0}) : alt_target — the
   non-JALR target is a register; nothing in the target mux depends on
   the compare. JAL never redirects any more; JALR always does.
   EX/MEM.pc_next stays the architectural next PC (RVFI-only, pruned
   from the timed netlist). EX/MEM.br_taken (BHT update only) =
   br_mp ^ pred, registered; it is a new endpoint at the same depth as
   the existing ones, not deeper.
   Also: a BRANCH never has reg_write/mem_read/mem_write set, so
   branch_trap should only set ctrl.is_illegal (RVFI-only) and leave the
   reg_write/mem_* clear term to mem_misalign | jalr_misalign. That takes
   the compare off the EX/MEM.ctrl.reg_write endpoint (path 1). It does
   not raise Fmax alone (the PC/kill_q twins remain), but it keeps the
   endpoint count on the compare chain from growing.

5. hazard_unit / forward_unit unchanged. When a valid instruction is
   captured into ID/EX, stall_if = 0 and redirect = 0, so the PC really
   followed ID/EX.pred_taken. On load-use / imem / dmem / div stall the
   PC holds and the word is refetched and re-predicted; a same-cycle EX
   redirect has priority and flush_id kills the predicted word.

Expected: ~289k fewer bubbles (as measured on r2s1, whose cycle count is
identical to r3s0) -> cycles ~4.24M (-6.4%). New IF paths (imem flop ->
1 LUT -> 32-bit carry -> 3 LUT -> PC; PC flop -> 128:1 BHT mux ->
pred_taken -> PC-mux select) start at flops that arrive ~2 ns before the
BSRAM DO and are ~4-5 levels shorter than the 11-level DO path, so Fmax
should hold at ~89 MHz (r3s2 even rose +5% on its base). Net ~+7%.
Implementer: run `make timing TARGET=bench` and confirm neither the
fetch_tgt adder nor the BHT read appears in the worst paths; if the BHT
read does, index it with a registered copy of next-PC bits instead.

changes.description: New module: 128 x 2-bit bimodal BHT (flops, sync reset 2'b01). Async read indexed by IF pc[8:2]; one write port indexed by EX/MEM.pc[8:2] with saturating update from the carried counter snapshot and the registered taken bit, enabled for a valid non-trapping BRANCH when !hold_mem_wb.

Raw-word predecode (legal BRANCH / JAL only), dedicated fetch adder pc + (instr[3] ? Jimm : Bimm), pred_taken = JAL or BRANCH with ctr[1], aligned target only. PC next = redirect ? redirect_target : (stall ? pc : pred_taken ? fetch_tgt : pc+4), redirect as the last mux level. Export pred_taken, ctr, fetch_tgt in if_id_t.
if_id_t: + pred_taken, bht_ctr, fetch_tgt. id_ex_t: + pred_taken, bht_ctr, alt_target. ex_mem_t: + bht_ctr, br_taken, br_upd (valid non-trapping BRANCH).

Register pred_taken and redir_const as kill_q side-effect bits (AND in.valid, cleared on flush/reset), the pred-flipped mispredict selects mp_eq/mp_ne/mp_lt/mp_ge (replacing br_eq/ne/lt/ge on the redirect path), bht_ctr, alt_target = pred_taken ? pc+4 : fetch_tgt; take br_target/br_misalign for BRANCH/JAL from fetch_tgt (keep the pc+imm adder for AUIPC). Hold all new fields on stall.

redirect = redir_const | br_ok & ((mp_eq & eq_v) | (mp_ne & ~eq_v) | (mp_lt & lt_v) | (mp_ge & ~lt_v)) using ID-precomputed mispredict selects (same LUT depth as r3s0); redirect_target = is_jalr ? (jalr_misalign ? link : {agu[31:1],0}) : alt_target. branch_trap only sets ctrl.is_illegal (not in the reg_write/mem_* clear). Latch br_taken, bht_ctr, br_upd into EX/MEM. pc_next unchanged (architectural).
Instantiate branch_predictor: read with the IF PC, write from EX/MEM (br_upd && valid && !hold_mem_wb). Wire the new IF/ID fields through.

Directed cases: warm backward loop (predicted taken, no bubble), forward not-taken branch, predicted-taken branch that falls through (mispredict to pc+4), JAL with no bubble, JALR, predicted branch in IF while EX redirects, predicted branch under imem/dmem stall and load-use stall; check architectural results and RVFI pc_rdata/pc_wdata continuity.

title: Cut the post-chain tails: unmerged ALU-group EX/MEM registers + branch compare folded into per-bit PC / kill LUT5s
motivation:
`make timing TARGET=bench` on r4s0 (place_option 0, 95.4 MHz, data path
10.445 ns = 15.774 - 5.329 clock insertion) shows two twin cones from the
regfile BSRAM DO (tC2Q 2.26 ns, arrives 7.589), within 0.035 ns of each other
(r2s0 lesson: break both or nothing moves):
A) ALU result (paths 1-11, 19): DO -> alu_b mux (fanout 72) 9.17 -> b^sub LUT
   10.56 -> carry chain -> sum[25] 12.307, then FOUR LUT levels of the
   per-bit result OR (alu_result_25_s13/s8/s2/s) -> EX/MEM.alu_result D
   15.774. The shifter variant (path 2: alu_b_1 fanout 74 -> 3 shifter
   stages -> 3 OR LUTs) ends at 15.773. So ~3.5 ns of every worst path is the
   result-merge tail AFTER the arithmetic is done.
B) Branch -> PC (paths 12-25, slack -5.446): DO -> rs2 mux 9.24 -> 33-bit
   compare chain br_diff[32] 12.059 -> net 1.1 -> take_pc_w_s2 13.73 ->
   take_pc_w_s1 (fanout 32) 14.19 -> net 0.98 -> pc_d LUT 15.740 -> pc D.
   3.7 ns after the compare: two LUTs to form take, then a fanout-32 net to
   the per-bit 2:1 PC mux. The take_kill -> kill_q copy has the same shape.
Every other path in the report has positive slack, so if both tails go the
next limit is ~1.5 ns shorter.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Same pipeline, same CPI (cycles must stay 4527646); only where merges happen.

A) Do not merge ALU result groups in EX. EX/MEM gets, instead of alu_result:
   - sum_q[31:0]  = raw adder sum[31:0] (carry chain SUM -> FF D, no LUT)
   - lt_q         = raw sum[32] (SLT/SLTU result bit)
   - rest_q[31:0] = sll_g | sr_g | logic_g | early (shifter group selects
                    stay folded into the shamt[4] stage; logic/early are
                    register-near), so the shifter cone ends one OR after
                    stage 3 instead of three
   - add_q / slt_q = registered alu_add / alu_slt group bits.
   The merge moves to register-sourced logic one cycle later (~2 ns ahead of
   the BSRAM DO, so it has slack):
   - Forwarding: split the one-hot opsel_t `ex` source into `exs` (producer
     in ID/EX has alu_add: take sum_q) and `exr` (any other forwardable
     producer: take rest_q, with bit 0 |= slt_q & lt_q). forward_unit already
     runs in ID against the ID/EX producer, so the split uses the registered
     ID/EX.alu_add bit; rs?_other / b_other stay one AND-OR of registered
     sources (exs&sum_q | exr&rest_x | wb | wl [| imm]) before the single
     2:1 against the DO.
   - MEM: nonload = is_mul ? mul : (add_q ? sum_q : rest_x); result =
     mem_to_reg ? load : nonload (load path unchanged: still one 2:1 from
     the dmem DO side).
B) Fold the branch condition into the consumers' last LUT, no `take` net.
   ID already registers br_ok/use_lt/inv. In EX, from registers / AGU only:
     P_i = br_ok ? (inv ? pc_alt_i : br_target_i) : pc_nt_i   (cond = 1)
     Q_i = br_ok ? (inv ? br_target_i : pc_alt_i) : pc_nt_i   (cond = 0)
   where pc_alt (stall ? pc : pc+4, or jump target) and pc_nt (jalr_go ?
   agu_target : pc_alt) are r4s0's existing nets (a non-branch has P = Q, so
   JAL/JALR/stall/sequential behaviour is unchanged). Then per bit
     pc_d[i] = (use_lt ? lt : eq) ? P_i : Q_i
   a 5-input function (use_lt, lt, eq, P_i, Q_i) = one Gowin LUT5
   (2xLUT4 + MUX2_LUT5), with lt/eq fanning out straight from the compare
   chain / XOR-reduce to the 32 PC bits (keep lt and eq as syn_keep nets,
   write pc_d so synthesis cannot re-extract a shared `take`). Same for the 9
   ID/EX kill bits: kill_d[k] = cond ? KP_k : kill_nt_k with
   KP_k = kill_nt_k & ~(br_ok & !dmem_stall). Expected new PC arrival ~14.0
   (chain 12.06 + ~1.2 net + LUT5 ~0.7) and JALR ~14.3 vs 15.74 today.
With both tails gone the EX worst paths drop ~1.3-1.7 ns (10.45 -> ~9.0 ns
data path), i.e. ~105-110 MHz median at unchanged cycles.

title: Flip-flop register file read in ID: take the regfile BSRAM out of EX at zero CPI cost
motivation:
The champion r4s0 (97.986 MHz, 4,527,646 cycles) is limited by
cpu/u_rf/regs_regs_0_0_s0 -> cpu/u_ex/u_alu -> EX/MEM.alu_result
(11 levels, arrival 15.77 ns). The start point is the regfile BSRAM.
ID/EX.rs?_val is the BSRAM's internal read register, so the operand
only reaches EX after the hard-block clock-to-out plus a long route
from the BSRAM column. Earlier notes measured this at about 2 ns later
than every other register, or about 3 ns of the period when routing
is included. r3s0 and r4s0 already cut everything after DO down to a
single 2:1 LUT, so no further micro-opt can remove what is left.
r3s1 and r4s1 tried to move the read into its own stage with an IF/ID
register. That cost about 2.8% in cycles (deeper redirect) and added
new paths into hard-block inputs, so it netted only +3.6%.
There is a zero-CPI way to do this that has not been tried. In the
timed netlist io_imemData is an LFSR flop (fpga/core_bench_si.sv;
noted in r3s2/r4s2), so a combinational regfile read in ID, addressed
by the raw fetched word, starts at a fast flop's clock-to-out. If the
regfile is built from ordinary flip-flops, not BSRAM or LUT-RAM, the
32:1 read mux runs in ID, which has slack. ID/EX.rs?_val becomes a
plain fabric FF that arrives with all the other EX inputs. The
pipeline timing is unchanged: the read is still addressed by the IF/ID
word in the same cycle and captured at the same edge. The cycle count
should therefore stay at exactly 4,527,646.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the BSRAM regfile with a 31x32 flip-flop array, x0 hardwired
to 0, using a combinational 32:1 read per port inside ID. Because the
read data is now an early fabric signal in ID, the write-first bypass
and the immediate can also be folded into ID. This removes the wl
(and, for ALU-B, imm) forwarding source from EX:
  rs1_reg_d = (w_en && w_addr == rs1 && rs1 != 0) ? w_data : rf[rs1]
  rs2_reg_d = same for rs2
  b_reg_d   = alu_src ? imm : rs2_reg_d
ID/EX latches rs1_reg / rs2_reg / b_reg; wl_val is deleted.
forward_unit drops the wl compare (it moves into ID as the bypass
compare above) and emits a 2-bit encoded select per operand,
priority EX/MEM > MEM/WB > reg. x0 falls through to reg, which reads 0
because rf[0]=0 and the bypass is suppressed for rs==0.
EX then has a 3:1 mux per operand bit, {ex, wb, reg}, with registered
encoded selects: s_reg ? reg : (s_wb ? wb : ex). That is a 5-input
function, so one LUT4 plus one MUX2_LUT5. It replaces the current
"AND-OR of other sources, then ram ? DO : other" structure. Keep the
r4s0 syn_keep duplicates (rs1 / rs1_sh / shamt_l / shamt_r / alu_b
copies) and every redirect and kill structure exactly as they are.
Expected timing: the old worst path loses the BSRAM excess
clock-to-out and column route (about 2 ns) and gains at most one
MUX2 (about 0.2 ns), so roughly 10.2 -> 8.5-9.0 ns, about 110-118 MHz.
New paths, all starting at fabric FFs:
  (a) EX/MEM.alu_result -> 3:1 mux -> ALU -> EX/MEM.alu_result
  (b) the branch compare -> take -> PC / kill
  (c) the ID read: LFSR imem flop -> rs field (high fanout) -> 32:1
      mux (LUT4 + MUX2_LUT5..8) -> bypass 2:1 -> ID/EX FF, about 5-6 ns
(d) dmem BSRAM DO -> load align -> MEM/WB.result, unchanged.
Cost: about +990 FF (666 -> about 1650 of 15.5k) and about +1100 LUT4
for two 32-bit 32:1 read ports (2163 -> about 3300, under the
10k target). Two regfile BSRAMs are freed (bsram 6 -> 4).
Implementation must-haves:
  1. The array must not be inferred as BSRAM or LUT-RAM. Use
     /* synthesis syn_ramstyle = "registers" */ and write it as 31
     explicit 32-bit registers (generate loop, per-register write
     enable = w_en && w_addr == i). Check the Gowin resource report:
     bsram must drop by 2 and lutram must stay 0. If Gowin retimes the
     ID/EX FF in front of an async read, as it did with LUT-RAM in
     r2s1, the gain disappears.
  2. If the read-address nets show up in the top paths, split the
     fanout of the IF/ID rs1/rs2 fields with syn_keep copies (for
     example one 5-bit copy per 8 data bits).
  3. Leave every hold and kill rule unchanged. The merged reg value is
     held with ID/EX on stall_id exactly as wl_val is today. On dstall,
     EX/MEM and MEM/WB also hold, so the ex/wb selects stay valid. A
     div latches its operands on its first EX cycle.
  4. Keep the initial zero fill for sim and formal parity. No reset on
     the array.
  5. The cycle count must be identical to r4s0 (4,527,646). Any
     difference means a forwarding or bypass bug.
If (a) or (b) at about 8.5 ns becomes the new limit, it is still
about 1.8 ns better than today's DO-prefixed version, so the gain does
not depend on finding further fixes.

title: Port IF predecode + bimodal BHT onto r4s0, prediction folded into the registered br_inv bit so redirect keeps r4s0's exact LUT shape
motivation:
The champion r4s0 (97.986 MHz, 4,527,646 timed cycles) still resolves
every taken BRANCH, JAL and JALR in EX. IF and ID share a cycle (no IF/ID
flop), so each taken control transfer costs one bubble: ~360k bubbles per

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Re-implement the r4s2 predictor on top of r4s0 (do NOT copy r4s2 RTL;
r4s0 restructured the PC mux into pc_alt / pc_nt / take and the ID/EX kill
into kill_nt & ~take_kill). Key structural rule: nothing new may be added
after the BSRAM DO -> compare chain; the prediction must only change
REGISTERED inputs of the existing take / jump / target logic.

1. rtl/branch_predictor.sv (new): 128 x 2-bit saturating counters as
   flops (no LUT-RAM), synchronous reset to 2'b01, indexed by pc[8:2].
   Async read from the IF PC register (use a syn_keep copy of pc[8:2]
   for the index so the 128:1 read mux does not load the imem/fetch-adder
   PC nets). One write port, indexed by EX/MEM.pc[8:2], enabled when
   EX/MEM holds a valid non-trapping BRANCH and the pipe advances
   (!hold_mem_wb); data = sat_inc/sat_dec of the counter snapshot carried
   down the pipe (if_id -> id_ex -> ex_mem) using a registered taken bit.
   Writing from EX/MEM keeps branch_cond off every predictor flop's D.

2. rtl/if_stage.sv: raw-word predecode and fetch target.
     fetch_is_br  = opcode==1100011 && funct3 not in {2,3}
     fetch_is_jal = opcode==1101111
     fetch_tgt    = pc + (instr[3] ? Jimm : Bimm)   -- dedicated adder,
                    immediate is a 1-LUT mux on raw instr bits
     pred_taken   = valid && ((fetch_is_jal && !Jimm[1]) ||
                              (fetch_is_br  && ctr[1] && !Bimm[1]))
   (misaligned targets are never predicted, so trap behaviour is
   unchanged). Keep r4s0's PC D-mux order exactly, with the prediction
   only inside the register-sourced pc_alt term:
     pc_alt = jump  ? (jalr ? link : br_target)
            : stall ? pc
            : pred_taken ? fetch_tgt : pc + 4;
     pc_nt  = jalr_go ? agu_target : pc_alt;
     pc_d   = take    ? br_target  : pc_nt;      -- take = last select
   Use a syn_keep copy of pred_taken for the PC mux and a separate one
   for ID, so the 32-bit PC mux fanout does not slow the ID copy.
   Export pred_taken and ctr in if_id_t.

3. rtl/id_stage.sv / rtl/core_pkg.sv: fold the prediction into the
   existing registered branch-condition and target fields, so EX's
   take logic is bit-for-bit the same shape as r4s0:
     - br_inv     <= branch_op[0] ^ pred_taken
       => take_pc = br_ok && ((use_lt ? lt : eq) ^ br_inv) now means
          "mispredicted" (actual != predicted). No new LUT after the
          compare; this is simpler than r4s2's four mp_* selects.
     - br_target  <= pred_taken ? pc + 4 : pc + imm   (the recovery PC;
       pc+imm is the existing ID adder, the mux select is an early IF
       signal). Keep an RVFI-only arch_target = pc + imm field for
       pc_next (pruned from the timed netlist).
     - jump kill bit (kill_q[2], drives `jump`, flush_id and pc_alt):
       becomes is_jump && !pred_taken, i.e. JALR only (and any JAL the
       IF did not predict, which a valid captured word never is). JAL
       no longer flushes or redirects.
     - pred_taken itself as a new kill_q side-effect bit (valid-gated,
       cleared on reset/flush/take_kill) plus bht_ctr[1:0] (data field,
       held on stall).
   Every new data field is held on stall_id exactly like the existing
   selects. Safety argument (also for formal liveness/unique): whenever
   a valid word is captured into ID/EX, stall_if = 0 and EX did not
   redirect (redirect kills the IF word via take_kill / flush_id), so
   the PC really followed ID/EX.pred_taken; load-use / imem / dmem / div
   stalls hold the PC and the word is refetched and re-predicted.

4. rtl/ex_stage.sv: unchanged take_pc / take_kill expressions (they
   already read br_ok, br_use_lt, br_inv). redirect (RVFI pc_next only)
   uses the architectural condition = mispredict ^ pred_taken and
   arch_target. EX/MEM gets bht_ctr, br_taken (= branch_cond ^ pred,
   a new endpoint at the same depth as EX/MEM.ctrl, not deeper) and
   br_upd (valid branch with br_ok). branch_trap keeps setting only
   ctrl.is_illegal, using the architectural condition.

5. hazard_unit / forward_unit unchanged (id_ex_jump is now the
   JALR-only kill bit, which only shortens flush_id).

Expected: cycles 4,527,646 -> ~4,238,604 (-6.4%, measured twice on
bases with the identical cycle count). New paths: LFSR imem flop ->
1 LUT imm mux -> 32-bit carry -> pred mux -> pc_alt -> pc_nt -> pc_d
(~6 levels from an early flop) and PC flop -> 128:1 counter mux ->
pred_taken -> pc_alt select (~6 levels) both stay well inside r4s0's
~10.2 ns, whose critical cones start ~2 ns later at the BSRAM DO and
are untouched. Fmax ~96-98 MHz -> fitness ~228-231 (+5.5..+6.8%).
