lesson: - 2026-10-01 hyp-20261001-003-r5s2 (regression, -12.62%): Re-implementing the IF predecode + 128x2b flop BHT on r4s0 with the prediction folded into registered br_inv / br_target / kill bits added nothing after the BSRAM DO, yet it still lost 12.62%: since fitness = Fmax*1e7/cycles, 189.11 means ~80 MHz at the expected 4.24M cycles and at most ~85.6 MHz with no CPI gain, both below r4s2's ~87.9 MHz on the slower r3s0, so this port made a path that is longer in absolute terms, not just a fetch path that r4s0's tighter period exposed (candidates are PC -> 128:1 BHT mux -> pred_taken as a select inside the 32-bit pc_alt -> pc_nt -> pc_d chain after the imem -> fetch-adder carry chain, and the 32-bit `pred_taken ? pc+4 : pc+imm` recovery mux after the ID adder; the cycles/Fmax split and timing_paths were not logged), so a path that starts at an early flop is not automatically short, and a predictor port onto r5s1's ~9.65 ns period should be planned from that run's timing_paths, not from earlier ports' Fmax deltas.

title: Cut five twin r5s1 critical paths at once: flop-only DSP inputs, split late high-fanout nets, one-LUT take/stall tails
motivation:
`make timing TARGET=bench` on r5s1 (place option 0, 100.1 MHz) lists 25
setup paths, all within 0.17 ns of each other (arrival 15.11-15.28 ns,
clock arrival 5.33 ns). They fall into five independent cones, so
fixing one alone gains nothing (lessons r2s0 and r4s0):
 P1 (15.282) EX/MEM.ctrl.alu_op[4] -> 2 LUTs (op decode, sign AND,
    2.6 ns with routes) -> DSP A[34] (fanout 72) -> DSP 3.76 ns ->
    2 LUTs (case(op) lo/hi, is_mul/mem_to_reg chain) -> MEM/WB.result.
    The extended operand bit is a LUT output, so it cannot be packed as
    a flop in front of the DSP.
 P6 (15.247) ID/EX.sel_a.wb (fanout 32, 1.81 ns route) -> rs1 3:1 mux
    as 2 LUTs (fanout 15, 2.33 ns route) -> br_diff carry chain ->
    take_pc_w as 2 LUTs (fanout 32, 1.11 ns route) -> pc_d -> PC.
 P16 (15.173) ID/EX.alu_sub (fanout 34) -> 4.83 ns route to the adder's
    carry-in sum_0/CIN -> chain -> 4 LUTs of result tail.
 P11 (15.221) ID/EX.rd -> hazard rd==rs compare chain -> stall_if as
    2 LUTs -> pc_alt_30_s5 (fanout 11) -> pc_alt 2 LUTs -> pc_nt ->
    pc_d, i.e. 5 LUTs from stall_if to the PC D input.
 P22 (15.125) EX/MEM.alu_result -> rs1 mux 2 LUTs (fanout 15, 2.71 ns
    route) -> SLL shifter -> 6 LUTs -> EX/MEM.alu_result.
None of these needs a CPI change. Each has 1-4 ns of avoidable delay:
routes of high-fanout control flops, or LUT levels that only decode
registered state after the late signal.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Apply five zero-CPI fixes together. Cycles must stay exactly 4,527,646;
any difference is a bug.
A. MUL (P1). ID decodes and registers mul_a_sgn (MULH/MULHSU),
   mul_b_sgn (MULH), mul_lo (MUL) and mul_hi (MULH/MULHSU/MULHU). EX
   latches the extension bits into EX/MEM: mul_ax = mul_a_sgn & rs1[31]
   and mul_bx = mul_b_sgn & rs2[31] (rs1/rs2 are the post-forward
   values). It also latches the one-hot MEM result selects sel_mlo,
   sel_mhi, sel_ld and sel_alu, with sel_mlo / sel_mhi cleared on
   ex_busy bubbles exactly like is_mul. mul_unit then multiplies
   $signed({mul_ax, rs1_val}) * $signed({mul_bx, rs2_val}) with no op
   decode, so every DSP input is a flop. mem_stage merges
   ({32{sel_mlo}} & lo) | ({32{sel_mhi}} & hi) | ({32{sel_ld}} & load)
   | ({32{sel_alu}} & alu), so each DSP output bit is one LUT4 from
   the final OR. ALTOPS keeps its case(op) stand-ins on
   EX/MEM.ctrl.alu_op in the ifdef branch only.
B. Adder carry-in (P16). Split alu_sub into two ID/EX flops (syn_keep /
   syn_preserve): alu_cin, which feeds only the sum's +sub carry-in
   (fanout 1), and alu_sub, which feeds the b XOR. Duplicate the
   ID/EX operand-select flops, one copy per EX operand-mux copy, so no
   select flop drives more than about 16 loads (sel_a.wb today drives
   32).
C. Branch -> PC (P6). Add dedicated syn_keep comparator copies rs1_cmp
   and rs2_cmp, from their own select-flop copies, that feed only
   br_diff and the eq reduce. This takes the compare loads off the
   fanout-15 rs1 net. Make take a single LUT after br_diff[32]:
   take = lt ? t_lt : t_nlt, where t_lt = br_ok & (use_lt ? !inv :
   eq ^ inv) and t_nlt = br_ok & (use_lt ? inv : eq ^ inv) are formed
   in parallel from eq and registered bits. Emit take_pc as two
   syn_keep copies (PC[31:16] and PC[15:0]), plus take_kill, so no
   copy drives 32 loads.
D. Load-use stall -> PC (P11). Register lu_arm = (mem_read | is_mul)
   & rd != 0 in ID (one ID/EX flop), so load_use = lu_arm & (rd==rs1 |
   rd==rs2). Restructure the PC D mux so the stall is one 2:1 select
   on register-only data: pc_reg = jump ? (jalr ? link : br_target) :
   pc + 4 (registers only), pc_alt = hold ? pc : pc_reg with hold =
   stall_if & !jump, then pc_nt = jalr_go ? agu_target : pc_alt and
   pc_d = take ? br_target : pc_nt. That is 3 LUTs after stall_if
   instead of 5. Keep the "redirect overrides stall" priority.
E. Forward -> shifter (P22). Split the shifter operand copy rs1_sh into
   rs1_sll and rs1_sr, and keep shamt_l / shamt_r, each from its own
   select-flop copy, so each copy drives about 8 loads and can be
   placed next to its shifter.
Expected: the longest of the five cones drops by at least 0.6-1.0 ns
(P1 by about 2.5 ns, P16 by about 3 ns, P6/P11/P22 by about 0.7-1.2
ns). That gives 9.65 -> about 8.8-9.0 ns, or 107-113 MHz (+4-10%)
at about +150 FF and +100 LUT. Paths outside the visible top 25 may
cap the gain, so confidence is low. The implementing agent should
re-run `make timing TARGET=bench` and check that all five cones moved.

title: Decoupled fetch: 2-entry fall-through instruction queue keeps fetching through back-end stalls
motivation:
A fresh `make timing TARGET=bench` on the r5s1 champion (100.1 MHz with placement
option 0, data delay ~9.95 ns) shows a flat timing wall. Four
independent EX-centred families are within 0.2 ns of each other:
  - EX/MEM.ctrl.alu_op -> mul sign LUTs -> 33x33 DSP -> result mux ->
    MEM/WB.result (15.282 ns)
  - ID/EX.sel_a.wb (fanout 32) -> rs1 3:1 mux -> 2.3 ns route ->
    br_diff carry chain -> take_pc (2 LUTs) -> pc_d (15.247 ns)
  - sel_a.wb -> rs1 mux -> 4-level LUT shifter -> result OR ->
    EX/MEM.alu_result (15.187 ns)
  - alu_sub / EX/MEM.alu_result fwd -> adder -> alu_result (15.12-15.18 ns)
Cutting any one family gains nothing. Cutting all four is micro-opt
work, and r5s0 already lost -7% on that ground. The structural lever
that is still unused is CPI. Both buses stall on a free-running LFSR
(bench_stall_gen: an independent 22% per cycle, whether or not a
request is pending). Today `stall_if` holds the PC, and the
fetched word is thrown away, on every back-end stall: load-use,
MUL-use, dmem stall, divider busy. So every cycle the back end
stalls while imem was ready is a lost fetch. A later imem-not-ready
cycle then costs a full bubble. Rough count for CoreMark: about 24k
dstall cycles plus 15-20k load/MUL-use bubbles per iteration (out of
about 453k cycles). In about 78% of those cycles imem is ready, so
about 30k fetch slots are wasted per iteration.

hypothesis.motivation:
A fresh `make timing TARGET=bench` on the r5s1 champion (100.1 MHz with placement
option 0, data delay ~9.95 ns) shows a flat timing wall. Four
independent EX-centred families are within 0.2 ns of each other:
  - EX/MEM.ctrl.alu_op -> mul sign LUTs -> 33x33 DSP -> result mux ->
    MEM/WB.result (15.282 ns)
  - ID/EX.sel_a.wb (fanout 32) -> rs1 3:1 mux -> 2.3 ns route ->
    br_diff carry chain -> take_pc (2 LUTs) -> pc_d (15.247 ns)
  - sel_a.wb -> rs1 mux -> 4-level LUT shifter -> result OR ->
    EX/MEM.alu_result (15.187 ns)
  - alu_sub / EX/MEM.alu_result fwd -> adder -> alu_result (15.12-15.18 ns)
Cutting any one family gains nothing. Cutting all four is micro-opt
work, and r5s0 already lost -7% on that ground. The structural lever
that is still unused is CPI. Both buses stall on a free-running LFSR
(bench_stall_gen: an independent 22% per cycle, whether or not a
request is pending). Today `stall_if` holds the PC, and the
fetched word is thrown away, on every back-end stall: load-use,
MUL-use, dmem stall, divider busy. So every cycle the back end
stalls while imem was ready is a lost fetch. A later imem-not-ready
cycle then costs a full bubble. Rough count for CoreMark: about 24k
dstall cycles plus 15-20k load/MUL-use bubbles per iteration (out of
about 453k cycles). In about 78% of those cycles imem is ready, so
about 30k fetch slots are wasted per iteration.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Decouple IF from ID with a 2-entry instruction queue that has a
fall-through path, so fetch keeps running while the back end is
stalled.
- The fetch PC `fpc` advances on `fetch_ok = imem_ready && space_q`.
  `space_q` is a registered "queue has room after this cycle" flag
  (count_q < 2, depth 2). Redirect stays the last D-mux select:
  pc_d = take ? br_target : (jalr_go ? agu_target : (jump ? (jalr ?
  link : br_target) : (fetch_ok ? fpc+4 : fpc))). stall_if no longer
  contains load_use_hazard, dmem_stall or ex_busy. The PC hold depends
  only on registered queue state and the imem_ready flop, which also
  takes the hazard compare off the PC path.
- ID sees `q_empty_q ? {fpc, io_imemData, imem_ready} : head entry`.
  The select is registered, so this adds one 2:1 LUT level at the
  start of the ID path (imem word -> regfile 32:1 read / decoder /
  imm / forward and load-use compares). That path is not in the top
  25 today, so it has some slack. In the zero-stall case the queue
  is empty and behaviour is cycle-identical to today: same redirect
  penalty and same forwarding distances.
- Push: a word fetched with imem_ready while ID does not consume
  (stall_id, load-use flush, or the queue already non-empty) is
  written into the queue with its PC. Pop: when ID/EX captures and
  the queue is non-empty. Count and pointer next-state use only
  registered terms plus the consume signal. The late `take` /
  jump-flush clears the queue as the last AND term (r4s0 rule: no
  CE/SR from a late signal).
- On a redirect (taken branch, JAL/JALR in EX), the queue is emptied
  and the current ID word is killed exactly as today. Wrong-path
  queued words are never captured.
- Hazard_unit: load_use_hazard/flush_id and the forward_unit compares
  now take rs1/rs2 from the ID-visible word (queue head or imem). The
  rest of the hold/kill rules are unchanged. stall_id keeps
  dmem_stall || ex_busy. A dequeue happens only when ID/EX actually
  captures a valid word (not on load-use flush, not on stall).
Expected effect: about 30k extra fetches per iteration land during
back-end stalls. About 2/3 of them are consumed before the next
taken redirect flushes them, and each consumed one hides a later
imem-not-ready bubble, so roughly 18-24k cycles per iteration (4-5%)
are saved. The EX/MEM wall (mul, branch -> PC, shifter, adder)
is untouched, so Fmax should hold at about 100-104 MHz, provided the
extra ID-entry 2:1 LUT stays off the critical set. If the ID path
does become critical, duplicate the rs1/rs2 field nets (syn_keep)
after the mux, as r5s1 suggested for the read-address fanout.
Implementation must-haves:
  1. Keep RVFI pc_rdata/pc_wdata correct: each queue entry carries
     its own PC, and ID uses the entry PC for link / br_target /
     AUIPC.
  2. Liveness: fetch never blocks forever. space_q is set whenever
     count_q < 2, and a pop always frees a slot by the next cycle.
  3. Do not let `take` drive any queue CE or sync reset; fold it in
     as the last AND on count/valid D inputs, as with kill_q.
  4. Cosim cycles must drop. Log the CoreMark cycle count against
     4,527,646 in implementation_notes.

lesson: - 2026-10-01 hyp-20261001-002-r6s1 (regression, -4.03%): A 2-entry fall-through instruction queue that keeps fetching through load-use/MUL-use/dmem/divider stalls lost 4.03% to its r5s1 base even though the zero-stall behaviour was argued to be cycle-identical; since fitness = Fmax*1e7/cycles, 219.68 means ~99.5 MHz at the unchanged 4,527,646 cycles and ~95 MHz at the predicted 4-5% cycle cut (vs ~103.6 MHz; the split was not logged), so Fmax fell by at least as much as the CPI could return, most likely because the q_empty_q head-vs-imem 2:1 mux now sits in front of r5s1's combinational 32:1 flop-regfile read (whose zero-CPI win relied on the ID word being a bare imem flop) and the load-use compare on that muxed word now also drives consume -> push/pop/count; so on r5s1's flat timing wall, an ID path that is "not in the top 25" has no real slack, one extra LUT level on the ID front end (~0.4-0.5 ns of ~9.65 ns) costs about as much as a hand-estimated 4-5% CPI gain, and any fetch-buffer idea must keep the regfile read address a single flop or count that LUT level against its gain.

title: Ahead-pipelined bimodal BHT (prediction is a flop, table read off the PC loop) + IF predecode zero-bubble JAL/taken-branch on r5s1
motivation:
IF and ID share a cycle and every taken BRANCH / JAL / JALR still resolves
in EX, costing one bubble each (~360k of r5s1's 4,527,646 timed cycles).
r3s2 / r4s2 / r5s2 all measured that IF predecode + a dedicated fetch adder
+ a 128x2b bimodal BHT cuts cycles to 4,238,604 (-6.38%). Every port lost
Fmax, and r5s2's log shows why: its worst path was the loop
pc_idx_q -> u_bht (128:1 read) -> pred_taken -> pc_alt/pc_nt/pc_d ->
pc_idx_q (15 cells, 16.4 ns, 80 MHz). The table read sat INSIDE the
single-cycle PC recurrence. In the timed netlist (fpga/core_bench_si.sv)
io_imemData is an LFSR flop and io_imemAddr only feeds the LED XOR. So once
the table read is out of the loop, every remaining predictor path starts at
an early fabric flop and needs at most two LUT levels before the PC muxes.
r5s1's current worst path is EX/MEM.alu_op -> mul_unit DSP -> MEM/WB.result
(6 cells), which the predictor does not touch. At unchanged Fmax:
228.91 * 4527646 / 4238604 = ~244.5 (+6.8%). Break-even for the 4.6% bar is
~101.5 MHz (-2.1%).

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Port the proven CPI mechanism onto r5s1, but make the prediction bit a
REGISTER. Then nothing on the PC D-input path reads the table.

1. Ahead-pipelined BHT (new rtl/branch_predictor.sv, or inside if_stage):
   128 x 2-bit saturating counters as flops (no LUT-RAM, no BSRAM),
   zero-filled by an `initial` block (or sync reset to 2'b01) for sim and
   formal determinism. The read is indexed by the CURRENT PC flop
   (a syn_keep copy of pc[8:2]). Its MSB and the index go into
   pred_q / idx_q through a plain D-mux that holds on stall_if:
     pred_d = stall_if ? pred_q : ctr[pc[8:2]][1];  idx_d likewise.
   When the PC advances from A to B, pred_q = BHT[A] and idx_q = A[8:2], so
   they describe the instruction fetched next (index = previous fetch
   address: a deterministic path hash; the update reuses the same index).
   The 128:1 mux now ends at pred_q and never feeds a PC mux. Holding on
   stall_if keeps the random 22% imem stalls from changing the index of a
   given branch. A redirect during a stall may leave a stale but
   self-consistent {pred_q, idx_q} pair. That costs a little accuracy but
   never correctness.

2. IF predecode of the fetched word (if_stage.sv):
     f_br   = opcode==1100011 && funct3 not in {2,3}
     f_jal  = opcode==1101111
     ptake  = (f_br && pred_q && !instr[8])  ||   // Bimm[1] = instr[8]
              (f_jal && !instr[21])                // Jimm[1] = instr[21]
     f_tgt  = pc + (instr[3] ? Jimm : Bimm)        // dedicated adder; the
              // immediate is a 1-LUT mux on raw instr bits, not imm_gen
   Misaligned targets are never predicted. That matches ID (JAL misalign ->
   trapping non-jump) and EX (br_ok excludes misaligned), so trap behavior
   is unchanged. The PC D-mux keeps EX `take` as the very LAST 2:1 select.
   f_tgt (adder output) is a DATA input of the level just before it, and
   its select sel_f = ptake && !stall_if && !jump is computed in parallel:
     pc_nt = jalr_go ? agu_target : pc_alt          (unchanged)
     pc_f  = sel_f   ? f_tgt      : pc_nt
     pc_d  = take    ? ex_tgt     : pc_f
   (pc_f and pc_d can pack as LUT4 + MUX2_LUT5 per bit.) ex_tgt =
   p_q ? link : br_target is selected from ID/EX flops, so it is early.
   Use syn_keep copies of sel_f and take for the 32-bit fanout. Never put
   ptake or pred_q in front of the fetch adder (no pc + (p ? imm : 4)).

3. ID / EX verify (id_stage.sv, ex_stage.sv, core_pkg.sv):
   ID/EX latches p = f_br && pred_q && !instr[8] (what IF acted on, by the
   same expression) and bht_idx = idx_q, held on stall_id like the other
   data fields. A valid, un-killed capture implies !stall_if && !jump &&
   !take, so p is exactly IF's decision.
   Fold p into a SECOND registered inversion bit used only by the take
   copies: br_inv_t = branch_op[0] ^ p. Then
   take = br_ok && ((use_lt ? lt : eq) ^ br_inv_t) stays one LUT after the
   compare chain. Keep the original br_inv for branch_trap and RVFI
   pc_next (actual outcome; pruned from the timed netlist).
   JAL is always taken in IF, so EX no longer redirects for it.
   `jump` / flush_id / the PC pc_alt jump term become JALR-only
   (is_jump && is_jalr, registered in ID as its own kill bit).
   Keep ID's existing pc+imm adder (br_target, AUIPC) unchanged. Do NOT add
   a `p ? pc+4 : pc_imm` mux after it (r5s2's suspected second long path).

4. Counter update off all EX/IF paths: EX/MEM gets upd_v (valid,
   non-trapping BRANCH), upd_idx and upd_taken (actual cond, one LUT after
   the compare, into a flop). In the MEM cycle, when upd_v && !hold_mem_wb,
   do a fresh flop RMW: read ctr[upd_idx] (128:1 x 2), saturating inc/dec,
   one-hot write enable. Fresh reads (not a fetch-time snapshot) keep
   tight loops whose branch refetches before the previous update from
   using stale counters.

Correctness: EX checks every prediction against the actual outcome, so any
BHT content (including formal's symbolic initial state) is legal. RVFI
fields are unchanged. Expected ~4.24M cycles at ~103 MHz, about +6%
fitness.

lesson: - 2026-10-01 hyp-20261001-003-r6s2 (regression, -1.93%): Moving the 128:1 BHT read out of the PC recurrence into an ahead-indexed pred_q/idx_q flop pair (index = previous fetch address, held on stall_if) removed r5s2's 15-cell pc_idx_q -> u_bht -> PC loop, but the IF predecode predictor still was not Fmax-neutral on r5s1: since fitness = Fmax*1e7/cycles, 224.50 means ~95.2 MHz (10.51 ns, +0.86 ns over r5s1's 9.65 ns) if cycles reached the expected 4.24M, and ~101.6 MHz even with no CPI gain (the split and timing_paths were not logged), so what is left of a same-cycle fetch redirect (imem flop -> opcode predecode / B-J imm mux -> 32-bit fetch-adder carry chain -> pc_f -> pc_d, with sel_f also gated by stall_if's load-use compare on the imem word) is itself longer than r5s1's flat ~9.65 ns wall; this is the third predecode port in a row (r4s2, r5s2, r6s2) whose Fmax loss ate the 6.4% cycle cut, so on these ~9-10 ns bases a predictor pays only if every PC-mux data input and select comes straight from flops (for example a taken bit and a target both read one cycle ahead into registers, as pred_q is here, with no fetch adder in the PC loop), and the next attempt should log the cycles/Fmax split and top timing_paths before porting again.

title: Cut r6s0's whole 9.0 ns wall at zero CPI: adder sum straight to an EX/MEM flop, carry-chain PC+4, AUIPC via br_target, 8-bit take copies
motivation:
`make timing` on r6s0 (109.96 MHz on place_option 0; the period is
9.06 ns of data delay) shows a flat wall of five distinct cones within
0.15 ns. In each one, synthesis-chosen LUT depth, not the carry chains,
sets the delay:
 1. MEM/WB.result_0 -> rs1 fwd mux (2 cells) -> ALU adder carry chain
    (bit 0 -> 27, only 1.0 ns) -> FIVE LUT levels of result-OR tail
    (alu_result_27_s19/s15/s10/s3/s, about 4.0 ns after sum_27/SUM) ->
    EX/MEM.alu_result_27 (9.06 ns). Synthesis put the adder sum at the
    HEAD of the chain that also merges the shifters / logic / early.
 2. PC_5 -> `pc + 4` -> pc_26 (9.06 ns): Gowin built the +4 as a 5-LUT
    ripple incrementer (n62/n59/n56/n49/n42, about 5.1 ns), not a carry
    chain, followed by the pc_reg -> pc_alt -> pc_nt -> pc_d LUTs.
 3. instr flop -> decoder/imm (3 LUTs) -> pc_imm carry chain -> imm_val
    (AUIPC mux) -> b_reg (alu_src mux) -> ID/EX.b_val_18 (9.04 ns).
 4. sel_b_shl_q -> shamt_l mux (2) -> SIX LUT levels of shifter + merge
    tail -> EX/MEM.alu_result_25 (9.04 ns).
 5. EX/MEM.alu_result_8 -> rs2_cmp mux -> br_diff chain -> t_lt ->
    take_hi_w (fanout 16, 2.0 ns route) -> pc_d (8.97 ns); the take_kill
    copy -> ID/EX kill_q RESET is 8.92 ns.
r6s0's lesson says a fix pays only the gap to the next tier, so all five
have to be cut together. Each has a structural fix that costs no cycles.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Four RTL-only, cycle-identical fixes (cycles stay 4,527,646):
A. EX/MEM ALU result split (cones 1 and 4). Replace EX/MEM.alu_result with
   add_q (D = adder sum, gated by the registered alu_add select under the
   existing !stall enable, so the sum reaches the D pin with at most one
   LUT2 or with the gate on the DFF's sync reset; bit 0 also takes
   alu_slt & sum[32] in that one LUT) and oth_q (D = sll_g | sr_g |
   logic_g | early as ONE LUT4 over syn_keep'd group outputs; each shifter
   is three explicit mux stages with the group select folded into the
   shamt[4] stage). Consumers OR them back together:
     - the EX forward source becomes add_q | oth_q inside every existing
       operand-mux copy: rf ? val : (wb ? mem_wb : add_q | oth_q), that is
       LUT4(wb, mem_wb, add_q, oth_q) and the rf branch joined by the same
       MUX2_LUT5 as today, so the forward-mux depth does not change.
     - MEM: ID clears alu_add for loads (it is set today because a load's
       alu_op is ADD), so add_q and oth_q are 0 for loads and MUL*, and
       result = mul_out | (sel_ld & load_data) | add_q | oth_q, the same
       5 inputs per bit as today's merge, with sel_alu dropped.
   Cone 1 loses about 4 ns (5 tail LUTs become 0-1). Cone 4 loses the
   extra LUT levels that synthesis built when it merged the sum in.
B. PC incrementer (cone 2). Make `pc + 4` a real carry-chain adder (for
   example pc[31:2] + a syn_keep'd 30-bit constant-1 operand, or another
   form that stops Gowin from building a LUT ripple). That takes it from
   about 5.1 ns to about 2 ns. Share the same incrementer with ID's link
   (in.pc == pc). If needed, fold `hold` into pc_reg so one LUT less
   follows the incrementer.
C. AUIPC through the early group (cone 3). ID/EX.br_target already
   latches pc + imm, so AUIPC selects a new registered alu_auipc term in
   EX's early merge (early = link&alu_link | div&alu_div |
   br_target&alu_auipc, all register-sourced). The imm_val mux goes away:
   ID/EX.imm = imm and b_val = alu_src ? imm : rs2_reg, so the pc_imm
   carry chain and one LUT leave the b_val path (about 2 ns). Only
   br_target still ends after the pc_imm adder, and it has no extra
   muxes after it.
D. Branch take fanout (cone 5). Split take_pc_hi / take_pc_lo into four
   syn_keep copies, one per 8 PC bits (fanout 8 instead of 16, about
   1 ns of route instead of 2.0 ns). Keep take_kill as a D-input AND on
   kill_q (syn_keep on kill_nt, as now). If Gowin still maps take_kill
   to the RESET pin, give it its own syn_keep'd LUT copy per 5 kill bits.

tier, which `make timing` does not list (top-25 floor 8.91 ns). Expect
about 115-120 MHz.

title: End-of-cycle forwarding: EX operands become bare flops (forward mux moved behind the ALU), plus shallow result tail
motivation:
`make timing TARGET=bench` on the r6s0 champion (place option 0, 109.96 MHz,
period ~9.06 ns data delay) shows a flat top-25 wall (9.06 -> 8.91 ns) made
of five cone types. Three of them begin with the same structure, the
start-of-EX forwarding mux:
  P1/P5-P7 (9.06): MEM/WB.result (fanout ~45: 31 regfile D pins + ~12
    operand-mux copies) -> rs1 3:1 mux as 2 LUTs (Q->mux out = 1.9 ns,
    then a ~1.0 ns route) -> 28-bit carry chain -> FIVE LUT levels of
    result-OR tail (sum_27 at 10.37 ns -> alu_result_27 D at 14.39 ns,
    ~4 ns after the carry), i.e. the late adder sum entered the deepest
    level of the OR tree, not the last one.
  P4/P8/P9 (9.04): sel_b_shl / sel_a_sr / EX/MEM.alu_result -> shamt or
    rs1_sll / rs1_sr 3:1 mux (2 LUTs) -> shifter -> 5-6 LUTs -> alu_result.
  P13-P16, P22-P24 (8.97 / 8.92): EX/MEM.alu_result_8 -> rs1_cmp mux ->
    br_diff chain -> take -> PC D, and -> kill_q RESET pins (synthesis
    turned the take_kill D-term back into a sync reset).
The other two are front-end cones:
  P2/P10/P25 (9.06): pc -> `pc + 4` mapped as a 5-LUT ripple (n62..n42)
    instead of a carry chain -> pc_reg -> pc_alt -> pc_nt -> pc_d.
  P3/P11/P12 (9.04): imem word -> decoder/imm_gen (3 LUTs) -> pc+imm carry
    chain -> AUIPC imm_val mux -> b_reg mux -> ID/EX.b_val.
Every ALU / shifter / compare cone pays ~2.9 ns for start-of-EX
forwarding (2-LUT 3:1 mux on high-fanout flops + its fanout-16 output
route) before any useful work starts. Lessons r5s1/r6s0 say each cone
fixed alone pays only the gap to the next tier, so all five must move.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Restructure forwarding so that it happens at the END of the producer's
cycle, into the ID/EX operand registers, instead of at the START of EX.
The EX stage then reads bare (duplicated, low-fanout) operand flops
straight into the adder, the shifters, the AGU and the branch compare.

1. End-of-cycle (ID-side) forwarding. For the instruction C in ID at
   cycle n, every ID/EX operand copy (rs1 main lo/hi, rs1_sll, rs1_sr,
   rs1_cmp, rs2 lo/hi, rs2_cmp, alu_b lo/hi, shamt_l, shamt_r) captures
     next = hit_ex ? alu_out_comb(EX, producer P1)
          : hit_mem_alu ? EX/MEM.alu_result (flop, producer P2)
          : rf_val (flop-regfile read + write-first bypass, as today)
   hit_ex / hit_mem come from forward_unit's existing ID compares (IF/ID
   rs vs ID/EX.rd / EX/MEM.rd). The inner 2:1 (mid = hit_mem_alu ?
   EX/MEM.alu_result : rf_val) settles in parallel with the ALU. The final
   select must be built so the late ALU outputs enter only the LAST LUT:
   per operand copy precompute A = hit_ex ? rest_g : mid (rest_g = the
   pre-gated logic | early | shifter groups) and Bsel = hit_ex & sel_add,
   then next = A | (Bsel & sum) (one LUT3 after the carry chain). The
   same LUT feeds EX/MEM.alu_result's D through its own copy
   (alu_result = (sel_add & sum) | rest_g, syn_keep on rest_g), which also
   fixes the 5-LUT tail on its own. Each copy's select pair gets its own
   syn_preserve flop or LUT as today so no net exceeds ~16 loads.
   P1 = LOAD or MUL is still caught by the existing lu_arm 1-bubble
   interlock (C is killed in ID/EX and recaptures next cycle, when the
   producer is P2).
2. P2 = LOAD / MUL (the only value not available from a flop or the ALU
   at the end of cycle n): the dmem BSRAM DO / DSP output must NOT be
   routed into the operand flops (lesson r3s0: keep late hard-block
   outputs one LUT from their consumer). Instead ID/EX latches a one-hot
   bit ldfwd per operand copy (hit_mem && EX/MEM is load/mul), the
   captured value is forced to 0, and EX ORs in a dedicated, syn_preserve
   MEM/WB copy of the load/mul result: op = op_q | (ldfwd_q & wbld_q),
   one LUT3 whose inputs are all local flops (the wbld copy has fanout
   <= ~12; the regfile write keeps its own MEM/WB.result copy). This
   replaces today's LUT4+MUX2 3:1 on two fanout-45/fanout-12 sources.
   EX/MEM -> EX forwarding and MEM/WB -> EX forwarding of ALU results
   disappear from EX entirely. CPI is unchanged (same bypass coverage,
   same 1-bubble load/MUL-use interlock).
3. Divider: latches its operands from the bare EX operands (+ldfwd OR)
   exactly as today; `early` (link, div result) is unchanged.
4. Front-end cones, so the gain is not capped by them:
   - AUIPC no longer folds pc+imm into b_val: ID/EX.br_target (= pc+imm,
     already registered) is OR-ed into the register-sourced `early`
     group under a new alu_auipc select, so b_val = alu_src ? imm : rs2
     has no carry chain in front of it.
   - PC: keep a registered pc_plus4_q (= pc_d + 4 computed on a carry
     chain from the same D mux, or equivalently increment with an
     explicit carry-chain adder) so the sequential next PC is a flop in
     the PC D mux; order the PC mux so that the register-only terms are
     merged first and hold / jalr_go / take are the last 2:1 selects.
   - Keep take_kill as a D-input AND (add syn_keep on the kill_d term so
     Gowin cannot remap it to the kill_q RESET pins).
Expected critical paths after the change: ALU loop ~flop -> LUT3 ->
carry -> 1 LUT -> fanout-~12 route -> flops (~6.5 ns); shifter loop
~LUT3 + 3 shift levels + 1-2 LUTs (~7.5-8 ns); compare -> take -> PC
~7.5 ns (no 3:1 mux, no high-fanout source). Target ~8.2-8.4 ns
(~120 MHz) at unchanged 4,527,646 cycles, i.e. about +8-10% fitness.
The new longest cone is expected to be the shifter or the ID regfile
read -> mid mux -> operand flop path; the implementer should log the
cycles/Fmax split and the top timing_paths.

lesson: - 2026-10-01 hyp-20261001-002-r7s1 (regression, -10.88%): Moving forwarding to the end of the producer's cycle (each ID/EX operand copy captures `hit_ex ? ALU sum/rest : hit_mem ? EX/MEM.alu_result : regfile`, and load/MUL results are OR-ed in EX from a MEM/WB wbld copy under a registered ldfwd bit) relocated the bypass mux instead of removing it from the 1-cycle ALU loop: since fitness = Fmax*1e7/cycles, 215.81 at the unchanged 4,527,646 cycles means ~97.7 MHz (9.12 -> ~10.23 ns, +1.1 ns), against r6s0's 109.6 MHz and r7s0's 119.7 MHz in the same round, likely because the loop still runs flop -> ldfwd OR LUT -> carry chain -> select LUT and now sends the late sum into ~12 operand-copy LUTs plus EX/MEM, while the combinational 32:1 flop-regfile read in ID (which r6s1 showed has no slack for even one extra LUT) gained the mid and A mux levels in front of the operand flops (the split and timing_paths were not logged); so a forward mux in the single-cycle ALU loop costs the same at either end of the cycle, and the cheaper fix is to shorten the logic around it as r7s0 did (sum one LUT from its consumers, +const on a carry chain), never adding LUT levels after the ID regfile read.

title: Ahead-indexed offset BTB: flop PC increment (pc + inc_q), verify imm==off in ID, no take in the table index
motivation:
Every taken BRANCH/JAL still costs one bubble. r6s2 measured that removing it
cuts cycles 4,527,646 -> 4,233,064 (-6.5%). But all three IF-predecode ports
(r4s2, r5s2, r6s2) lost more Fmax than that. The logs show two separate causes:
(1) imem flop -> predecode -> B/J imm mux -> fetch adder -> PC mux, plus
sel_f gated by stall_if, is longer than r6s0's ~9.1 ns wall;
(2) r6s2's worst path was EX/MEM.alu_result -> compare -> take -> pc_idx_q
(15.6 ns vs r6s0's 14.39 ns). The table-index PC copy took the late `take`
as its D-mux select, and its Q drove the 128:1 read trees, so P&R placed it
near the table, far from EX.
To be Fmax-neutral, a predictor must avoid both causes:
- no instruction-word logic and no new mux level in the PC recurrence;
- no flop next to the table with `take` (or the JALR AGU) in its D cone.
At unchanged Fmax, a 5% cycle cut gives about +5.3%. The break-even for the
4.6% bar is about -0.7% Fmax at -5.3% cycles.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Next-fetch-offset predictor read one fetch ahead. The only PC-loop change is
replacing the constant 4 in `pc + 4` with a flop.

1. Table (new rtl/fetch_pred.sv). 64 entries, each
   {v, ctr[1:0], tag[3:0], off[15:2]} (off = signed word offset).
   Use LUT-RAM (async read) or flops. The read is indexed by a DEDICATED
   index flop idx_q (pc[7:2]; tag pc[11:8]) with D = if_stage's pc_alt.
   pc_alt = hold ? pc : (jump ? jtgt : pc + inc_q), which contains neither
   `take` nor jalr_go/agu. So idx_q equals PC, except in the cycle after a
   take/JALR redirect, and no late signal reaches the table side.
   Lookup: hit = v && tag == idx_tag && ctr[1].
   Registered prediction for the NEXT fetched instruction (D-mux holds on
   `hold`):
     pq_q   = hit
     inc_q  = hit ? sext(off)<<2 : 32'd4
     pk_q   = {idx, hit, ctr}   (training key and snapshot)
   inc_q feeds ONLY the PC adder: pc_reg = jump ? jtgt : pc + inc_q.
   This is the same carry chain as today's pc+4, with a flop operand. There
   is no new mux level, and the table read is not in the PC loop.
   jtgt = jlink ? link : br_target is a LUT3 of ID/EX flops.
   Do NOT clear pq_q/inc_q with take. A stale prediction after a redirect
   is corrected by the verify step below.

2. Verify in ID (id_stage.sv). The inputs are the raw imem word plus flops;
   no adder is involved.
     bj_off = instr[3] ? Jimm[15:2] : Bimm[15:2]   (1 LUT on raw bits)
     imm_ok = (bj_off == pq_off) && imm[1]==0 && imm fits in [15:2]
     p_ok_br  = pq && is_branch && imm_ok
     p_ok_jal = pq && is_jal(aligned) && imm_ok
     p_bad    = pq && !p_ok_br && !p_ok_jal && !ctrl_decoded.is_jump
   These are registered into ID/EX:
   - br_inv_t = branch_op[0] ^ p_ok_br. The take copies then compute
     br_ok && (cond ^ p_ok), still one LUT after br_diff[32].
   - p_ok syn_preserve copies (hi/lo) select ex_tgt = p_ok ? link : br_target,
     a flop LUT3. take stays the LAST 2:1 select of pc_d.
   - is_jump kill bit = (dec_is_jump && !p_ok_jal) || p_bad.
   - jlink = is_jalr || p_bad.
   A p_bad instruction (wrong offset, non-branch alias, or a stale
   post-redirect prediction) is not killed. It executes normally and
   jump-redirects to link (pc+4). A p_bad branch that is actually taken is
   overridden by take -> br_target. A correctly predicted JAL is no longer
   a jump.
   RVFI redirect/pc_next uses an RVFI-only arch_jump bit (original

lesson: - 2026-10-01 hyp-20261001-003-r7s2 (regression, +4.69%): An ahead-indexed offset predictor whose only PC-loop change replaces the constant in `pc + 4` with a flop (inc_q) beat its base, which no predictor had done since r4s2; its table index flop is fed from pc_alt before the take/JALR selects, ID checks each prediction by comparing the raw B/J imm bits with the predicted offset (folded into br_inv_t, so take stays one LUT after br_diff), and a bad prediction is not killed but retires and jumps to link; since fitness = Fmax*1e7/cycles, 253.51 means ~109.0 MHz at the expected ~4.30M cycles and still ~107.3 MHz at r6s2's 4,233,064, against r6s0's 109.6 MHz (the split was not logged), so following r6s2's two rules (no instruction-word logic or new mux level in the PC recurrence, and no table-side flop with take or the JALR AGU in its D cone) is enough to keep a predictor near Fmax-neutral on a ~9 ns base; it lost only to r7s0's zero-CPI +9.21% in the same round, so port it onto r7s0 next, but expect a somewhat larger Fmax cost there, because `pc + inc_q` is a carry chain by construction and probably gave r6s0 part of r7s0's pc+4 carry-chain fix for free, and r7s0 already has that gain.

title: Cut r7s0's flat 8.7 ns wall at zero CPI: un-merge take copies, carry-free jalr_go, 16-load shifter selects, 4:1-mux shifters, AGU operand copy, flop-bounded divider negates
motivation:
`make timing` on r7s0 (place_option 0, 114.26 MHz; seeds 114.3/119.7/119.7)
lists 25 setup paths within 0.13 ns (8.58-8.72 ns of data delay). They fall
into at least seven distinct cones, and several are long only because of
fanout/structure that synthesis introduced, not because of real logic:
 1. sel_a_sll_q (fanout 32!) -> rs1_sll fwd mux (2 LUT) -> FIVE LUT levels
    of SLL shifter (sll_g_*_s9/s5/s4/s3/s5, ~0.4-0.95 ns route per hop) ->
    alu_oth_out LUT -> oth_q (8.72 ns). Same for SR from sel_a_sr_q
    (fanout 32, 2.07 ns first route) and from rs1_val / oth_q sources
    (paths 2, 4, 10, 12, 15, 19, 25).
 2. sel_a_lo_q -> rs1 mux (fanout 10) -> agu_sum[0..1] -> jalr_go
    (pc_nt_31_s2, FANOUT 30, 1.44 ns route) -> pc_nt -> pc_d (8.71 ns).
    jalr_go = is_jalr && !agu_sum[1] puts a carry-chain output on the
    select of the whole 32-bit PC mux.
 3. sel_a_cmp_q -> rs1_cmp mux -> 33-bit br_diff chain -> t_lt ->
    take_b0_w with FANOUT 33 -> ID/EX kill_q RESET and pc_d (8.69 ns):
    Gowin merged the four take_b*/two take_k* syn_keep copies into one
    LUT because they are logically identical.
 4. sel_a_lo_q -> rs1 (fanout 10) -> AGU carry chain -> dmem BSRAM ADB
    (paths 9, 11, 14, 20, 23; 8.68 ns).
 5. Divider: oth_q -> rs1 -> `a_neg ? -a : a` -> quo_q (paths 13, 17, 21)
    and is_rem_q -> `neg ? -sel : sel` -> early -> oth_q (path 18), i.e.
    two 32-bit negate chains inside the single-cycle EX loop for an op
    CoreMark's timed loop almost never executes.
The r6s0/r7s0 lessons say a micro-opt round pays only if every cone of the
wall is cut together, and r7s0's +0.77 ns came from removing multi-hop
tails rather than single levels. Each cone above has a zero-CPI (or, for
the divider, ~zero-CPI) fix.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Six RTL-only changes; cycles stay at 4,527,646 apart from at most +2
cycles per DIV/REM (none on the CoreMark hot path):
A. Un-mergeable take copies (cone 3). Give each take copy (4 PC-byte
   copies + 2 kill copies) its OWN syn_preserve ID/EX copy of the
   registered branch bits it reads (br_ok / br_use_lt / br_inv, or
   directly a per-copy {t_lt_q, t_nlt_q} pre-form built in ID from
   use_lt / inv / br_ok where eq is the only EX term), so the six LUTs
   have different input flops and synthesis cannot collapse them into one
   fanout-33 net. Each copy then drives 8 PC bits or 5 kill bits (route
   ~0.6 ns instead of ~1.5 ns). Keep take as the last D-mux select and the
   kill as a D-input AND (if Gowin still maps it to the DFF RESET pin,
   that is fine as long as the net fanout is 5).
B. Carry-free jalr_go (cone 2). Compute the JALR misalign bit
   agu_sum[1] = rs1[1] ^ imm[1] ^ (rs1[0] & imm[0]) on a small side path
   (from a dedicated 2-bit rs1 operand-mux copy with its own select flop,
   not off the AGU carry chain), and build jalr_go in four syn_keep
   per-PC-byte copies (fanout 8 each), each also on its own registered
   is_jump&&is_jalr flop copy. Architectural behaviour is unchanged
   (aligned JALR -> agu_target, misaligned -> trap + link); the select
   now settles ~1 LUT after the operand mux, well before the AGU high
   bits that are the mux data.
C. Shifter select fanout (cone 1). Split sel_a_sll / sel_a_sr into
   per-16-bit syn_preserve copies (lo/hi), as r6s0 did for the main rs1 /
   rs2 / alu_b copies; sel_b_shl / sel_b_shr already drive only 5 bits.
   Removes ~1-1.5 ns of first-hop route on paths 1 and 4.
D. Shallower shifters (cone 1). Rewrite each shifter as three explicit
   mux stages written as case-on-2-bit-select 4:1 muxes (shamt[1:0],
   shamt[3:2]) so Gowin maps each to 2xLUT3 + MUX2_LUT5 (one routed hop
   per stage), then the shamt[4] 2:1 stage with the group select folded
   in, then the existing oth LUT4. Target: 3 routed hops after the
   forward mux instead of 5. For SRL/SRA build the fill per stage from
   the registered arith bit and a_sr[31] (no 33-bit $signed trick), so
   the sign bit is not a high-fanout tail inside the stages.
E. AGU operand copy (cone 4). Give the AGU its own syn_keep rs1 copy
   (rs1_agu, own lo/hi select flops), so the rs1 net that feeds the adder,
   logic group, divider and MUL operand flops no longer also loads the
   AGU chain (rs1 fanout 10 -> ~6, rs1_agu fanout 1-2).
F. Divider negates out of EX (cone 5). At start latch the raw post-forward
   operands and sign flags (no negate between the forward mux and quo_q /
   dvs_q); take magnitudes in one extra "prep" cycle from those flops.
   After the last iteration, compute neg ? -sel : sel in one extra "fix"
   cycle into a result_q flop that feeds `early`, so early is
   AND-OR of flops only again. Handshake (start/idle/done/ack, ex_busy
   from registered state) is unchanged; ALTOPS branch keeps its 1-cycle
   done so riscv-formal liveness is unaffected. +2 cycles per DIV/REM.
With every listed cone cut by 0.6-1.5 ns, the period should fall to the
next unlisted tier; r5s1/r6s0/r7s0 each found that tier 0.5-0.8 ns down.
Expect ~8.0 ns data delay -> ~125-128 MHz median (+5-7%).

lesson: - 2026-10-01 hyp-20261001-001-r8s0 (regression, -4.93%): All six zero-CPI cone cuts (per-copy take/kill flops that synthesis cannot merge, a carry-free jalr_go in 4 copies, lo/hi copies of the shifter selects and shift amounts, explicit 4:1 shifter stages, an AGU rs1 copy, and the divider negates moved into extra prep/fix cycles; +78 FFs, +131 LUT4s) made placement option 0 only 1.6% faster (r7s0 114.26 -> 116.05 MHz locally), and that run's wall came back flat within 0.01 ns on PC-recurrence cones this round did not shorten (MEM/WB result forward -> EX -> PC over 34 cells, stall LFSR -> hazard -> PC hold, PC -> PC); the scored median of three placement seeds still fell from 119.7 to 113.8 MHz, so the two placements that gave r7s0 119.7 dropped to at most 113.8; r7s0's own 5% seed spread (114.3/119.7/119.7) shows that placement noise on this flat wall is now larger than one micro-opt round can gain, so compare a round against the same placement option its path list came from (r7s0's list came from option 0, its worst seed), time all three options locally before predicting, and do not read r7s0's +9.2% as a pure RTL gain.

title: Hide bus stalls off the EX wall: dual-path fetch skid (select after the ID bypass LUT) + posted 1-entry store buffer
motivation:
`make timing` on r7s0 (119.7 MHz median, 4,527,646 cycles) shows a flat wall: the top
paths are within 0.04 ns of each other and run through four different EX-loop cones
that all begin at the forward-mux select flops: SLL/SR shifter -> oth_q, rs1 AGU ->
JALR -> PC, branch compare -> take -> PC / ID-EX kill_q, and rs1 AGU -> dmem BSRAM ADB.
A stage split or any single-cone fix cannot move that wall (r3s1, r4s1 and r7s1 all
failed), so a structural win now has to come from cycles, and it must not add logic
to any of those four cones or to the ID front end. The largest cycle loss that is not
branch prediction is bus backpressure: imem_ready / dmem_ready are random flops that do
not depend on requests (fpga/bench_stall_gen.sv, about 22% low). With
P(ready) = 0.78, every fetch costs on average 0.28 extra cycles, and so does every
LOAD/STORE in MEM. Today, when ID is stalled (load-use or MUL-use interlock,
dmem stall, divider), the PC holds and a word the imem did deliver is thrown away and
fetched again, so the refetch can stall again. A STORE that sees dmem_ready=0 also
freezes the whole pipeline, although nothing later depends on when it is
written. r6s1 measured a 3.5% cycle cut from a 2-entry fetch queue but lost more in
Fmax, because its head/imem 2:1 mux sat in front of the combinational 32:1 regfile read
address (one extra LUT level on an ID front end with no slack).

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add two stall-hiding structures and keep every new mux select a flop that sits at the
END of an existing cone, never at its start.

(1) Fetch skid (1 entry, upgrade to 2 if timing allows): skid_v_q / skid_instr_q / skid_pc_q / skid_pc4_q.
When ID cannot accept the word this cycle (load-use/MUL-use flush, stall_id) and
imem_ready=1 and no redirect is taken, latch the delivered word into the skid and let the
PC advance (pc + 4). While the skid is valid, ID consumes the skid word and the imem keeps
fetching one word ahead. A refill in the same cycle is allowed, so after a stall the core runs
in "skid mode" with one word in reserve. In that mode an imem_ready=0 cycle costs nothing: ID
takes the skid word, the skid empties, and the core is back in direct mode. Any EX redirect
(taken branch, JAL/JALR) clears skid_v. That path already kills the ID word, so the
redirect penalty stays 1 cycle in both modes.
IMPORTANT (r6s1 lesson): the regfile read address must NOT be muxed. Add a second
regfile read pair (rs1/rs2 32:1 read of skid_instr_q) and a second decoder / imm_gen /
forward_unit compare / load-use compare on skid_instr_q. Those cones start at a flop and run in
parallel with the imem cones. The registered use_skid_q (= skid_v_q) then selects between the two
pre-formed ID results as the LAST level before each ID/EX D input. For the operand values, put it
after the write-first bypass LUT so it maps as a MUX2_LUT5 of two LUT4 outputs, which adds only
about 0.1-0.2 ns to that path. Because the skid cones start at a flop that settles early, they have
slack. Expect about +1000 LUT4 (budget 10000, now 3512). The hazard_unit load_use term
becomes use_skid_q ? lu_skid : lu_imem, again a final 2:1 on a flop select.

(2) Posted store buffer (1 entry): sb_v_q, sb_addr_q, sb_wdata_q, sb_wen_q. If a STORE is in
MEM, dmem_ready=0 and the buffer is empty, the store moves into the buffer and the
pipeline does NOT stall. It still retires that cycle (RVFI mem_* fields come from
EX/MEM as today). The buffer drains on the first cycle with dmem_ready=1 in which MEM holds no
memory op. drain_sel is computed from flops only (sb_v_q & !EX/MEM.mem_op). It selects
io_dmemAddr/WData/WEn between the buffer and EX/MEM after their flops, so the AGU still
ends at a fabric flop. The
rs1 AGU -> dmem BSRAM wall cone gets shorter, not longer, because ADB is no longer
absorbed. A LOAD or STORE that reaches MEM while sb_v_q=1 uses the port directly unless
its word address equals sb_addr_q (flop-to-flop compare). On a match it stalls exactly like a
dmem stall until the drain, which prevents a RAW hazard through memory. A second store
with dmem_ready=0 while the buffer is full stalls as today.
dmem_stall therefore becomes ex_mem_mem_op & (!dmem_ready & !(store & !sb_v_q) | sb_hit), where
every term is a flop or a flop compare. It must stay ahead of br_lt_v at the take_kill
gate. The MMIO markers (0x1000_01xx) are STOREs and may be posted too. Because the timing window
is bracketed by those writes, the drain ordering does not change what is measured.

Expected cycles: (1) the skid hides one imem-stall cycle per decode-stall event when the
refetch would have missed (~0.22 per event, ~2.5-3.5% of cycles, cf. r6s1's 3.5%). (2) The
store buffer removes almost all STORE dmem-stall cycles (~0.28 x STOREs, ~1.3-2%). Total
~4-5% fewer cycles, with Fmax kept within ~1% because no wall cone gains a level.

title: Port r7s2's ahead-indexed offset predictor onto r7s0 (inc_one -> inc_q), without the take -> inc_q squash that made r7s2's 36-cell path
motivation:
Every taken BRANCH and JAL on r7s0 still costs one bubble, because it
resolves in EX while IF and ID share a cycle. r7s2 measured what removing
most of these bubbles is worth on this pipeline: cycles went from 4,527,646
to 4,245,356 (-6.24%, log.jsonl). Its median Fmax fell only ~1.8% against
its r6s0 base (107.6 vs ~109.6 MHz), and its logged worst path (seed 0,
91 MHz) shows where that loss came from:
  MEM/WB.result_2 -> u_ex -> u_bp/inc_q_13, 36 cells
That is the EX forward mux (1) + the 33-cell br_diff carry chain + take
(1) + the inc_q D mux (1). The implementation squashed the registered
prediction with the late branch `take` (to drop stale predictions after a
redirect). That put EX's compare chain into a flop that sits beside the
table, far from EX. r6s2 hit the same failure with pc_idx_q. Remove that
term, and nothing late enters the predictor.
r7s0 makes this port cheaper than it was on r6s0. r7s0 already forces
`pc + 4` onto a carry chain as `pc[31:2] + inc_one`, where inc_one is a
syn_keep'd constant. Replacing that kept constant with a flop (inc_q)
leaves the same carry-chain cell structure in the PC recurrence, with no
new LUT or mux level. r7s0's worst paths are the EX shifter/ALU cones
(sel_a_sll_q -> oth_q, 8.35 ns), which the predictor does not touch.
At r7s0's 119.744 MHz, 4.245M cycles gives 282.1 (+6.7%). The 4.6% bar is
cleared down to about 117.4 MHz (-2.0%).

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Re-implement r7s2's next-fetch-offset predictor on r7s0, keeping r7s0's
timing structure and following four strict rules:
  R1 no instruction-word logic and no new LUT or mux level in the PC
     recurrence;
  R2 no predictor-side flop (idx_q, inc_q, pq_q, pk_q, or any squash or
     valid bit that fans out to the table side) has take, take_kill,
     jalr_go, agu_sum or the br_diff chain in its D cone;
  R3 take stays the last 2:1 select of pc_d and of the ID/EX kill bits,
     still one LUT after br_diff[32];
  R4 nothing new after ID's regfile read, and nothing new after the ID
     pc_imm carry chain.

1. Table (new rtl/fetch_pred.sv). 64 entries {v, ctr[1:0], tag[3:0],
   off[15:2]} in LUT-RAM (async read, sync write; or flops), zero-
   initialized. The read address is a dedicated index flop idx_q
   (pc[7:2], tag pc[11:8]) with D = if_stage's syn_keep'd pc_alt
   (= hold ? pc : pc_reg). pc_alt contains neither take nor jalr_go, so
   idx_q equals PC except in the cycle right after a take/JALR redirect.
   hit = v && ctr[1] && tag == idx_q[tag]. Registered prediction for the
   NEXT fetched instruction, D-mux held on `hold`:
     inc_q = hold ? inc_q : ((hit && !jump) ? sext(off) : 30'd1)
     pq_q  = hold ? pq_q  : (hit && !jump)
     pk_q  = hold ? pk_q  : {idx_q, hit, ctr}      // training key/snapshot
   `jump` (ID/EX.is_jump kill bit) is a flop, so squashing on it is
   allowed. It drops the stale prediction after a JAL/p_bad/JALR
   redirect. The stale cases after a taken-branch or JALR redirect are
   NOT squashed. They are rare (a predicted-taken branch must sit exactly
   1-2 instructions after the stale index), and the ID verify below turns
   them into an ordinary 1-bubble correction.
   The table entry predicts the instruction fetched after its index
   address (path-indexed by the predecessor). This is exactly r7s2's
   scheme.

2. IF (if_stage.sv). Replace the syn_keep'd constant inc_one with
   inc_q[31:2] in pc_inc = {pc[31:2] + inc_q, pc[1:0]}. This is the same
   carry chain as today, with a flop operand. The pc_reg term stays a
   5-input function: pc_reg = jump ? jtgt : pc_inc, with
   jtgt = jlink ? link : br_target pre-merged from ID/EX flops (syn_keep).
   pc_alt and pc_nt are unchanged. The last level stays per-byte:
   pc_d = take[i] ? ex_tgt : pc_nt, with ex_tgt = p_ok ? link : br_target
   a syn_keep'd LUT3 of ID/EX flops (p_ok syn_preserve hi/lo copies).
   ID's link needs plain pc + 4, so add a SEPARATE kept-constant carry-
   chain incrementer (pc[31:2] + inc_one) that feeds only IF/ID.pc4 ->
   ID/EX.link. It is off the PC loop.

3. ID verify (id_stage.sv). Inputs are raw imem bits plus flops; there
   is no adder:
     bj_off   = instr[3] ? Jimm[15:2] : Bimm[15:2]
     imm_ok   = bj_off == pq_off && imm[1] == 0 && imm fits in [15:2]
     p_ok_br  = pq_q && valid BRANCH && imm_ok
     p_ok_jal = pq_q && aligned JAL && imm_ok
     p_bad    = pq_q && !p_ok_br && !p_ok_jal && !dec_is_jump
   These are registered into ID/EX:
     br_inv_t = branch_op[0] ^ p_ok_br    (used only by t_lt/t_nlt)
     p_ok copies, jlink = dec_is_jalr || p_bad
     is_jump kill bit = (dec_is_jump && !p_ok_jal) || p_bad
     arch_jump (RVFI-only) and kv = key valid
   Keep the original br_inv and arch_jump for branch_trap and the RVFI
   pc_next (pruned from the timed netlist). alu_link stays dec_is_jump,
   so a p_bad ADD never selects link as its result.
   A p_bad instruction is not killed. It retires normally and its jump
   redirects to link (a taken p_bad branch is overridden by take ->
   br_target, because p_ok = 0).
   DIV corner case: a p_bad DIV is a "jump" while ex_busy. Gate
   flush_id's jump term with !ex_busy (both registered) in hazard_unit,
   so the jump cannot kill the DIV that is iterating in ID/EX. The PC
   sits at link meanwhile, and the first post-div capture is flushed and
   refetched.
   Any table content, including formal's symbolic initial state, is
   therefore legal, and every instruction still retires.

4. Training, off every late path. EX/MEM gets upd_v (kv && valid &&
   (BRANCH || JAL) && no trap), upd_taken (the actual cond, one LUT after
   the compare, straight into the EX/MEM flop), upd_key/snapshot, and
   upd_off. The table is written in MEM, gated by !hold_mem_wb:
     - taken, offset fits: {1, hit ? sat_inc : (JAL ? 2'b11 : 2'b10),
       tag, off}
     - not taken with hit: sat_dec
     - p_bad: v = 0
   kv = 0 for an instruction whose key was loaded in the cycle after a
   take/JALR redirect. That uses a one-flop redir_q with D = its own
   syn_keep take copy || jalr_go, which fans out ONLY to the kv flop
   next to ID/EX (fanout 1, so no table-side pull).

Expected: cycles ~4.25-4.27M (r7s2 measured 4.245M; the unsquashed stale
cases cost <= ~0.3%), and Fmax 117-120 MHz. The PC carry chain, pc_reg,
pc_d and the take copies keep r7s0's exact LUT depth, and the new table
read path (idx_q -> LUT-RAM -> 4:1 bank mux -> tag/hit -> inc_q mux,
about 5 levels) starts and ends at predictor flops. That gives a fitness
of ~275-282 (+4..+6.7%). The implementer must log the cycles/Fmax split
and the top timing paths, and must run `make timing` to check that no
path into idx_q/inc_q/pq_q/pk_q contains u_ex cells.

lesson: - 2026-10-01 hyp-20261001-003-r8s2 (regression, +3.33%): Porting r7s2's ahead-indexed offset predictor onto r7s0 (pc + inc_q on r7s0's existing pc+4 carry chain, a raw-imm verify in ID, and a take-free idx_q) beat r7s0's 264.47 but missed the 4.6% bar that the hypothesis set for itself; since fitness = Fmax*1e7/cycles, 273.27 means ~116.0 MHz at r7s2's 4,245,356 cycles (~116.7 at 4.27M), a ~3.1% Fmax loss against r7s2's ~1.8% on r6s0, as r7s2's lesson expected once the base already has a carry-chain pc+4; the diff likely also added load to the latest net in r7s0's wall, because br_lt_v (br_diff[32]) now drives two more LUTs (take_r_w, which is logically identical to the take copies that r8s0/r8s1 found Gowin merges and feeds stale_q/redir_q, and the upd_taken training mux), and stale_q, a take-derived flop, was wired into u_bp even though the plan allowed only a fanout-1 redir_q into the kv flop (the split and timing_paths again were not logged); so if the predictor's ~6% cycle cut carries over, on r7s0's flat wall every new consumer of br_lt_v/take costs Fmax comparable to that cut, and the next port should take its training outcome and stale/kv bits from flops after EX, not from new br_lt_v or take LUTs.

title: Carry-select the PC recurrence: split branch-compare and pc+4 chains into parallel halves, per-byte hold copies
motivation:
r7s0 (264.47 = ~119.7 MHz x 4,527,646 cycles) is limited by the PC
recurrence. r8s0 shortened the shifter, AGU and take-fanout cones but came
back on a wall flat within 0.01 ns made of three cones it did not touch:
(a) MEM/WB.result / EX/MEM forward -> rs?_cmp mux -> 33-bit br_diff carry
chain -> take LUT -> PC D-mux (34 cells, most of them carry cells),
(b) stall flop -> hazard -> `hold` (fanout 32 + ID/EX) -> pc_alt -> PC, and
(c) PC -> 30-bit pc+4 carry chain -> pc_reg/pc_alt/pc_nt/pc_d -> PC.
Two of the three are long serial carry chains (from r7s0's lesson: the
multi-ns tails sit around carry chains, not in single LUT levels).
The CPI side offers no micro-opt worth 4.6%. A CoreMark ISS pair count
(2.94M instructions) found load/MUL-use bubbles = 240K (136K load->branch,
59K LW->load address, 32K MUL->R), only 3.9K store-data-only and 80 false
raw-field interlocks. Every remaining CPI loss needs a structural change,
so this micro_opt slot goes to cutting the carry depth of all three wall
cones in the same round (r4s0/r6s0/r7s0 rule: fix the whole wall at once).

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Zero-CPI and the same cycle count (4,527,646). Shorten every PC-recurrence cone:
1) Branch compare (ex_stage): replace the single 33-bit br_diff chain with
   two independent ~16-bit chains run in parallel on the existing
   rs1_cmp/rs2_cmp copies: lt_hi = signed/unsigned compare of bits
   [31:16] (17-bit chain with the br_uns extend bit), lt_lo = unsigned
   compare of bits [15:0] (16-bit chain), and eq_hi = ~|(a[31:16]^b[31:16])
   (LUT tree, parallel with the chains). lt = lt_hi | (eq_hi & lt_lo).
   Fold this into each take copy as one LUT5 (LUT4 + MUX2_LUT5):
   take = lt_hi ? t_lt : (eq_hi & lt_lo ? t_lt : t_nlt), or pre-form
   t_lo = lt_lo ? t_lt : t_nlt per copy so the final level is a LUT4
   {lt_hi, eq_hi, t_lo, t_lt/t_nlt}. The carry chain halves (~17 cells, not ~33).
   Do not add any new consumer of the chain outputs beyond the existing
   4 PC + 2 kill take copies (r8s1/r8s2 rule). branch_cond / branch_trap
   (RVFI / trap only) are recomputed from the same lt.
2) pc+4 (if_stage): carry-select the incrementer. lo = pc[15:2] + 1
   (14-bit chain on a kept constant-1 operand as now), hi0 = pc[31:16],
   hi1 = pc[31:16] + 1 (16-bit kept-constant chain in parallel), and
   c_lo = &pc[15:2] (2-level LUT tree in parallel). pc4[31:16] =
   c_lo ? hi1 : hi0. The serial chain depth drops from 30 to 16 bits plus
   one LUT, and the low half (no extra LUT) has more slack. IF/ID.pc4 /
   link use the same value.
3) hold (hazard_unit / if_stage): emit four syn_keep copies of
   hold = stall_if && !jump (one per PC byte, fanout 8 each, the same
   pattern as take_pc) plus a separate copy for stall_id, so the
   io_imemReady / io_dmemReady flop -> hold net no longer drives 32+ loads.
Expected: each cone loses ~0.5-1 ns of carry/route delay. The next tier
(sel_a_sll_q -> shifter -> oth_q, 9 cells, r7s0's option-0 worst path)
sets the floor, so the gain is ~0.4-0.6 ns of 8.35 ns: ~119.7 -> ~126-128
MHz (+5-7%) at unchanged CPI. The implementer should run `make timing`
on all placement options before and after, and log the cycles/Fmax split
and the top timing_paths, as LESSONS asks.

lesson: - 2026-10-01 hyp-20261001-001-r9s0 (regression, -12.30%): Carry-selecting the PC-recurrence cones (a 16-bit low compare chain choosing between two parallel 17-bit high chains for a<b and a<=b, a pc+4 split into a 14-bit low chain plus duplicate 16-bit high halves, and four syn_keep `hold` copies) cut the branch -> PC cone from 22 to 17 cells but dropped placement option 0 from r7s0's 114.26 to 106.39 MHz, and since fitness = Fmax*1e7/cycles, 231.95 at the unchanged 4,527,646 cycles means a ~105.0 MHz median against 119.7; the plan's `eq_hi = ~|(a^b)` selector was not a free LUT tree, because Gowin maps a 16-bit `==` onto its own 14-cell carry chain, which put it in series before take (103.08 MHz as planned), and the final wall shows that carry cells barely cost delay (a 31-cell compare -> take_kill path and an 8-cell stall -> hold -> PC path ended within 0.08 ns), while the untouched shifter and divider cones came back ~0.65 ns slower, likely from the extra chains' area and placement, and Gowin again merged the four take copies into one 32-load net; so on GW2A, do not count carry cells as path length or split a chain into parallel copies to shorten it (r7s0's lesson put the multi-ns cost in the LUT and route tails around the chains, not in the chains), and check the netlist for a hidden carry chain before using any wide equality or reduction as a late select.

title: Take the branch compare out of the PC loop: redirect from a registered EX outcome one cycle later, bubble won back by r8s2's ahead-indexed offset predictor trained only from flops
motivation:
r7s0 (264.47, 119.7 MHz, 4,527,646 cycles) sits on a flat wall where one
of the recurring worst cones is EX/MEM.add_q -> forward mux -> 33-bit
br_diff chain -> take -> PC / ID-EX kill (r8s1: add_q -> skid, 32 cells;
r8s2: add_q -> pc, 38 cells). Every front-end CPI idea since r4s2 died on
this cone: r8s2's predictor cut cycles 6.2% (4,245,490) but lost ~3.1%
Fmax (116.0 MHz) because it hung new consumers on br_lt_v / take; r8s1's
skid cut 3.4% but added a 7th take copy and lost more Fmax. As long as the
branch compare must reach the PC flop in the same cycle, any predictor or
fetch buffer adds load to the latest net in the design.

hypothesis.motivation:
r7s0 (264.47, 119.7 MHz, 4,527,646 cycles) sits on a flat wall where one
of the recurring worst cones is EX/MEM.add_q -> forward mux -> 33-bit
br_diff chain -> take -> PC / ID-EX kill (r8s1: add_q -> skid, 32 cells;
r8s2: add_q -> pc, 38 cells). Every front-end CPI idea since r4s2 died on
this cone: r8s2's predictor cut cycles 6.2% (4,245,490) but lost ~3.1%
Fmax (116.0 MHz) because it hung new consumers on br_lt_v / take; r8s1's
skid cut 3.4% but added a 7th take copy and lost more Fmax. As long as the
branch compare must reach the PC flop in the same cycle, any predictor or
fetch buffer adds load to the latest net in the design.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Structurally move branch resolution one stage later and make the PC loop
flop-sourced:
  1. EX computes the branch outcome as today but only latches it:
     take_q (syn_preserve copies, fanout <= 8) plus the correct-path
     target (br_target or link) into an EX/MEM-side redirect register.
     Nothing in EX's combinational cone reaches the PC, ID/EX kill or
     EX/MEM ctrl from br_diff any more; br_diff[32] drives only flops.
  2. In the following cycle the registered mispredict (take_q != pred,
     or JALR) is the last 2:1 select of the PC D mux and kills the two
     younger slots: the wrong-path instruction now in EX (its EX/MEM
     capture of valid / reg_write / mem_* / is_mul, its own jump and its
     divider start are gated by redir_q) and the word in ID (ID/EX kill
     bits). redir_q has priority over a wrong-path jump in EX and is held
     across a dmem stall. Mispredict penalty
     becomes 2 bubbles instead of 1, but every input of the PC mux and
     of the kill AND is a flop.
  3. To win the bubble back, port r8s2's ahead-indexed offset predictor
     (64-entry LUT-RAM, idx_q from pc_alt, PC = pc + inc_q on the
     existing carry chain, raw-imm verify in ID folded into br_inv_t)
     but train it and clear its kv/stale bits only from the registered
     take_q / EX/MEM fields, never from br_lt_v or a new take LUT.
     JAL always predicts once seen; backward loop branches hit at
     ~90%+, so correctly predicted taken branches cost 0 bubbles.
Expected: cycles ~4.30-4.35M (r8s2's 6.2% cut minus the second bubble on
residual mispredicts and cold misses), Fmax back to >= r7s0's 119.7 MHz
or better since the take -> PC / kill cone is gone from the wall
(remaining wall: ALU loop, stall -> PC hold, PC -> PC). Fitness
119.7e7 / 4.32M ~ 277 (+4.8%), more if the removed cone lets the
ALU-loop placement improve.

lesson: - 2026-10-01 hyp-20261001-002-r9s1 (regression, -8.41%): Registering the branch outcome (take_q/target_q, so that one cycle later redir_q is the last PC-mux select and the ID/EX kill and squashes the wrong-path instruction in EX) and winning the extra bubble back with r8s2's flop-trained offset predictor lost 8.41% against a predicted +5%; since fitness = Fmax*1e7/cycles, 242.23 means ~104.6 MHz at the predicted 4.32M cycles and ~109.7 MHz even at r7s0's predictor-free 4,527,646, and holding r7s0's 119.7 MHz would take ~4.94M cycles (+9%) (the split was not logged), so the likely cause is a loss on both sides: taking the compare -> PC/kill cone off r7s0's flat wall cannot raise Fmax past the other wall cones (ALU forward loop, stall -> PC hold, PC -> PC; the same single-path trap as r2s0), and the redir_q copies took on a large new fanout (PC bytes, ID/EX kill, EX/MEM valid/reg_write/mem_*/is_mul capture, the EX jump, the divider start, plus a hold term across dmem stalls), while the second bubble is now paid on every remaining redirect (every JALR return, which jalr_go used to resolve in 1, every unpredicted or mispredicted branch, cold table misses and p_bad), and the 4.30-4.35M estimate implicitly allowed only ~55-105K such events against r8s2's 282K-cycle saving; so a deeper redirect that doubles the penalty is a certain CPI cost for an Fmax gain capped by the next wall cone, and its cycle count, which cosim measures exactly, must be checked against the predictor's saving before synthesis.

title: Predicted-next-PC checked in EX with a registered (1-cycle-late) redirect: offset predictor with no EX net in the PC loop
motivation:
The predictor lineage r7s2 -> r8s2 cuts cycles by about 6.2%
(4,527,646 -> 4,245,490, log.jsonl), but every port so far lost Fmax
on the same cone. r8s2's median fell from 119.7 to 116.0 MHz (seeds
108.3/116.0/116.0 against r7s0's 114.3/119.7/119.7), and its worst
path was EX/MEM.add_q -> forward mux -> br_diff carry chain -> take ->
u_if/pc_28 (38 cells). r7s0's own wall (r8s0 lesson) is made of the same
kind of path: MEM/WB result forward -> EX -> PC (34 cells), stall ->
hazard -> PC hold, and PC -> PC. In r8s2 the predictor added work to
that cone: ID-verify bits folded into take, a p_ok target mux, a
take-derived stale/redir flop, and training muxes on br_lt_v. That
work is what cost the 3.1%.
r7s0 resolves every redirect in the same cycle as the compare, which
is why any prediction logic ends up after br_diff. Once a predictor
supplies the next PC, the EX resolve does not need to steer the PC in
the same cycle. It only has to detect a misprediction, and that result
can be registered. Deferring the redirect by one cycle removes every
EX carry-chain output (br_diff -> take, agu_sum -> jalr_go) from the
PC D input, the ID/EX kill bits and the predictor flops. The PC loop
then has only flop-sourced selects. Mispredicts and unpredicted taken
transfers pay 2 bubbles instead of 1. Correctly predicted ones pay 0.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Keep r8s2's ahead-indexed offset table, which has the only proven
CPI gain, but replace its ID raw-imm verify and same-cycle take
redirect with a general check in EX: compare the predicted next PC
against the actual next PC, and send a registered redirect.

1. Predictor (new rtl/fetch_pred.sv), as in r8s2: 64 entries
   {v, ctr[1:0], tag[3:0], off[15:2]} in flops or LUT-RAM, zero-init.
   It is path-indexed. idx_q holds the PC of the instruction being
   fetched (dedicated flop copy of pc). The entry it reads is
   registered into inc_q (the offset applied at the NEXT fetch).
     inc_q <= redir_q || hold ? (redir_q ? 30'd1 : inc_q)
              : (hit ? sext(off) : 30'd1)
   redir_q is a flop (see 3), so the squash-after-redirect has no
   late input. idx_q <= pc_d. Because pc_d no longer contains take
   or jalr_go (only flops and the PC carry chain), there are no
   stale-index cases, and r8s2's kv/stale_q/redir-from-take logic is
   not needed. key_q {idx, tag, hit, ctr} is loaded with the same
   enable as inc_q. kv_q = !redir_q is a flop-only squash. Both travel
   with the instruction through IF/ID -> ID/EX -> EX/MEM as the
   training key. Entries are only trained when kv = 1.

2. IF (if_stage.sv). Same carry chain as r8s2:
   pc_inc = {pc[31:2] + inc_q, pc[1:0]}. Keep the separate kept-
   constant pc + 4 chain for link (IF/ID.pc4).
     pc_alt = hold ? pc : pc_inc
     pc_d[i] = redir_q[i] ? rtgt_q : pc_alt  (one redir_q copy per
                                              PC byte, syn_preserve)
   The jump/jalr/jalr_go/take inputs and the pc_reg / pc_nt levels go
   away, so the PC loop has fewer levels than r7s0. hold = stall_if
   (the jump-overrides-stall term becomes redir_q overriding at the
   last level). IF/ID also carries pnpc = pc_inc (the predicted next
   PC of this instruction), latched into ID/EX. No logic is added after
   the ID regfile read or the ID pc_imm chain.

3. EX check (ex_stage.sv). Every instruction carries ID/EX.pnpc. All
   inputs below are ID/EX flops except br_lt_v and agu_sum:
     m_t   = br_target != pnpc       (32-bit XOR-reduce of flops, in
     m_l   = link      != pnpc        parallel with br_diff)
     BRANCH: mis = cond ? m_t : m_l, pre-formed as m_lt / m_nlt so
             mis_br is one LUT after br_diff[32] (same shape as take)
     JAL:    mis = m_t;   non-control insn: mis = m_l
     JALR:   mis = (agu_target != pnpc), or link != pnpc if misaligned
   A misaligned JALR (trap, rd not written) ALWAYS sets mis, even when
   pnpc == link. Otherwise its follower would forward the unwritten
   link value from EX/MEM, because its select was computed against
   the JALR's uncleared reg_write.
   Registered, with CE = !stall (dmem stall), so a mispredict that is
   detected while EX/MEM holds a stalled load/store, or that becomes
   pending while redir_q waits for the stall to clear, is not lost:
     redir_q copies (4 PC bytes + 2 kill + 1 predictor squash + 1
     EX/MEM squash, syn_preserve) <= valid && mis && !ex_busy &&
     !redir_q
     rtgt_q <= actual next PC (cond/jalr select of br_target / link /
     agu_target)
   While redir_q && dmem_stall, PC <= rtgt_q every cycle and ID/EX
   holds. The kill/squash takes effect on the first unstalled cycle.
   Each copy is a fanout-light flop. Nothing in the PC, kill or table
   cones reads br_lt_v or agu_sum.
   The cycle after a mispredict (redir_q = 1): PC <= rtgt_q, ID/EX
   captures a bubble (redir_q is the last D-AND of the kill bits,
   replacing take_kill), and the wrong-path instruction now in EX is
   turned into a bubble on its way into EX/MEM (valid, reg_write,
   mem_read/mem_write, is_mul/sel_m* cleared, as ex_busy does today).
   Its own mis term is gated by !redir_q, its divider start is gated,
   and ex_busy is gated by !redir_q (register-only). It is never a mem
   op in MEM, so dmem_stall cannot coincide with redir_q.
   forward_unit stays exact: the squashed instruction reaches EX/MEM
   with reg_write = 0, and the instruction behind it is killed.

4. Training from flops after EX (r8s2 lesson). EX/MEM latches
   upd_key (predecessor idx/tag carried from IF), upd_off =
   (rtgt - pc)[15:2] on a carry chain into a flop (EX/MEM.rtgt_q -
   EX/MEM.pc is computed in MEM, off every late path), and upd_taken
   = (rtgt_q != link) from flops in MEM. The table is written in MEM,
   gated by !hold_mem_wb: taken and the offset fits -> {1, inc ctr,
   tag, off}; not taken with a hit -> dec ctr; a hit on a non-control
   instruction (aliasing) -> v = 0. JALR is trained the same way, so a
   return whose call site is fixed in a hot loop predicts correctly.

5. RVFI: pc_wdata stays the architectural next PC (pruned from the
   timed netlist). The trap rules are unchanged: a misaligned taken
   branch or JALR traps and continues at link, and the EX check treats
   link as its actual next PC.

Expected: cycles ~4.27-4.31M. r8s2 measured 4,245,490 with
1-bubble mispredicts. Here mispredicts and cold entries cost +1
bubble, and one prediction is lost after each redirect. JALR returns
and stale-index cases are recovered. Fmax returns to r7s0's ALU-cone
wall (median ~119.7 MHz; seeds 1/2 were limited by
sel_a_sll_q -> oth_q, which this change does not touch). The
EX -> PC / kill cone that limited r7s0's seed 0 and all of r8s2 is
removed, so seed 0 should improve too. 119.7 MHz at 4.29M cycles is
~279 (+5.5%). The implementer must log the cycles/Fmax split, the
mispredict count from cosim, and the top timing paths, and must
confirm that no path into pc, idx_q, inc_q or the ID/EX kill bits
contains u_ex carry-chain cells.

lesson: - 2026-10-01 hyp-20261001-003-r9s2 (regression, -8.38%): A second, independently designed registered-redirect predictor (EX compares every instruction's ID/EX.pnpc with its actual next PC, and flop-only redir_q/rtgt_q steer the PC, the ID/EX kill bits and the table one cycle later, with training from MEM flops) scored 242.32, within 0.04% of r9s1's 242.23, and r9s1's split, now in log.jsonl (4,298,818 cycles; 104.13 MHz on all three seeds; worst path from the bus-ready lfsr through the u_id decoder/imm into ID/EX kill_q_10, 20 cells), shows that r9s1's lesson misplaced the cost: the 2-bubble redirect cost only ~53K cycles over r8s2's 4,245,490, inside both hypotheses' 4.27-4.35M estimates, so the whole loss is Fmax (119.7 -> ~104 MHz; at r9s1's cycle count, r9s2's fitness implies ~104.2 MHz, since its own split was not logged); the likely cause is that a deferred redirect brings its own bookkeeping (redir_q held across dmem stalls, ANDed into every ID/EX kill bit, and squashing the wrong-path instruction's valid/reg_write/mem_*/is_mul/divider start) into the stall -> hazard -> ID/EX capture cone that was already on r7s0's wall, and the seed spread collapsing (114/120/120 -> 104/104/104) marks a real logic path, not placement noise; so flop-sourced PC-mux selects do not make a predictor Fmax-free when the redirect state must also merge with the bus-ready stall in the kill/hold logic, and since two implementations agree, drop the registered redirect and go back to r8s2's same-cycle redirect (273.27, the best predictor result so far), removing only its extra br_lt_v/take consumers.

title: Flatten the PC next-state mux: fold JAL into take, drop the pc_reg level and !jump from hold, tree the dmem-stall CE nets
motivation:
r8s0's run of r7s0 (placement option 0) found a flat wall in which every
cone ends at the PC flop: MEM/WB result forward -> compare chain -> take ->
PC (34 cells), bench stall flop -> hazard -> hold -> PC, and PC -> pc+4
chain -> PC. r8s0 and r9s0 then shortened the parts at the cone starts
(take copies, carry-select compare), and the wall came back unchanged or
slower. Neither round shortened the part all three cones share, the PC
D-input mux, which is four cascaded 2:1 levels:
  pc_reg = jump ? (jalr ? link : br_target) : pc4   (LUT5)
  pc_alt = hold ? pc : pc_reg                        (hold = stall && !jump)
  pc_nt  = jalr_go ? agu_target : pc_alt
  pc_d   = take ? br_target : pc_nt
So the PC -> PC cone runs carry chain -> 4 LUT levels, and the stall cone
runs hold (which also waits for !id_ex_jump) -> 3 LUT levels. Two of these
levels exist only for JAL, and JAL selects the same br_target that `take`
already selects at the last level. Also, dmem_ready (one bench flop) feeds
the whole ID/EX enable (~400 FFs), the EX/MEM hold (~350 FFs), MEM/WB
valid, the kill bits, take_kill and the PC hold through a single
dmem_stall LUT, so the stall cone pays for a ~800-load net before any
logic. Per LESSONS r7s0, multi-ns tails sit around the chains, not in
them, and these are such tails.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Zero-CPI restructure of the PC next state and the stall nets (cycles must
stay exactly 4,527,646; check this in cosim with --istall --dstall before
synthesis):
1. Fold JAL into take. ID/EX gets a new kill-bit flop jal_q
   (= is_jump && !is_jalr, killed like is_jump) plus syn_preserve
   registered precomputes, so each take copy stays one LUT after br_diff[32]:
     t_lt  = jal_q | (br_ok & (use_lt ? !inv : eq ^ inv))
     t_nlt = jal_q | (br_ok & (use_lt ?  inv : eq ^ inv))
   A JAL then takes the br_target path at the last PC mux level, exactly
   like a taken branch. (JAL misalign is already turned into a non-jump in
   ID, and br_ok is 0 for a JAL, so take==1 for it is always a valid
   redirect.) The take_kill copies also kill the follower for JAL, which
   flush_id already does, so this is redundant but harmless.
2. Rebuild the PC D mux with 3 levels, and only 2 after the pc+4 chain:
     pc_base = jalr_q ? link : (stall_if ? pc : pc4)   (one LUT5, jalr_q
               and link are flops, stall_if is early)
     pc_nt   = jalr_go ? agu_target : pc_base           (unchanged)
     pc_d    = take ? br_target : pc_nt                 (take last, unchanged)
   jalr_q = is_jump & is_jalr is a registered kill-bit flop (new, own copy).
   The `jump ?` level and pc_reg disappear. hold no longer needs
   `&& !id_ex_jump`: JAL wins through take, aligned JALR through jalr_go,
   misaligned JALR through jalr_q -> link, all above the stall select, so
   redirects still override every stall (same semantics as today:
   redirect is not gated by dmem_stall, and ID/EX holds the jump so it
   re-issues the same target). Write pc_base as one expression and keep
   it with syn_keep, so Gowin maps it as LUT4+LUT4+MUX2_LUT5 and not as a
   chain. PC -> PC drops from chain+4 LUT levels to chain+LUT5+2; the
   stall cone drops the !jump term from hold.
3. Tree the dmem-stall nets. Keep 4-6 syn_preserve copies of the EX/MEM
   mem_op bit (mem_read | mem_write, latched beside ctrl) and form one
   dmem_stall copy per consumer group: ID/EX enable (low/high halves of
   the payload), EX/MEM hold, MEM/WB valid + take_kill gating + kill_nt,
   and the PC-side stall_if. Each copy is a LUT2 over distinct flops, so
   synthesis cannot merge them, and each drives ~150-200 loads instead of
   one ~800-load net. Likewise give stall_if (the PC-side term, 32 loads)
   its own copy of the imem_ready / load-use / ex_busy OR, separate from
   the copy that feeds flush_if / in.valid into the decoder-side ANDs.

and less route delay on the stall CE nets. The compare -> take -> PC cone
keeps its shape and gains nothing, so the gain is capped at the ALU-loop
cone (sel_a_sll -> shifter -> oth_q, r7s0's option-0 worst path). The
plan expects 119.7 -> ~124-126 MHz median at unchanged cycles.

result is compared option by option (LESSONS r8s0). Log the cycles/Fmax
split. Add no new consumer of br_lt_v or take beyond the existing six
copies (LESSONS r8s2).

lesson: - 2026-10-01 hyp-20261001-001-r10s0 (regression, -13.76%): Flattening r7s0's PC D-mux (JAL folded into take through registered tk_eq/tk_lt1/tk_nlt1 kill bits, a `jalr_q ? link : (stall_if ? pc : pc4)` first level, no !jump in hold) and splitting the dmem-stall CE net into six syn_preserve mem_op copies feeding separate stall_id/stall_ex_mem halves, take_stall and stall_kill nets lost 13.76%; since fitness = Fmax*1e7/cycles, 228.09 at the required unchanged 4,527,646 cycles means ~103.3 MHz (8.35 -> ~9.68 ns), a 1.3 ns loss, far more than r7s0's ~0.4 ns seed spread, so the rewrite made a real longer path, not placement noise (the split and timing_paths were not available); the likely culprit is the stall-net tree, because the single dmem_ready bench flop still drives every copy (now a die-wide net on the bus-ready -> hazard -> ID/EX kill/CE cone, which r9s1's worst path already showed is fragile), and on GW2A, where the two flops of a CLS share CE/SR, each extra CE net is a new control set that packs the ~750 pipeline flops less densely; this is the third zero-CPI micro-opt round on r7s0 in a row to lose more than the one before (r8s0 -4.9%, r9s0 -12.3%, r10s0 -13.8%), each adding copies or chains to the PC/stall cones, so stop duplicating control nets on r7s0, and diff any further PC/stall rewrite's timing_paths against r7s0's on the same placement option before scoring it.

title: Fold WB into MEM: regfile written from the MEM result, MEM/WB forward source becomes the ID bypass, EX operand muxes shrink to 2:1
motivation:
r7s0's wall (seen again in r8s0's path list) is flat across the PC-recurrence cones, and its
worst member is the 34-cell MEM/WB.result -> EX operand 3:1 mux -> branch compare chain -> take
-> PC path. The same 3:1 mux (rf ? ID/EX value : wb ? MEM/WB.result : EX/MEM add_q|oth_q) sits
at the head of every EX cone: ALU adder -> add_q, shifters -> oth_q, AGU -> dmem address,
compare -> take -> PC/kill. Each mux copy has 6 inputs per bit, so Gowin maps it to a LUT4 plus
a MUX2_LUT5 or two LUT levels, and twelve copies of it are the reason for the duplicated select
flops, the syn_keep copies and much of the routing congestion around EX. Prior rounds removed
LUT tails after carry chains (r7s0) but never removed a whole forward source; r7s1 only moved
the mux to the other end of the cycle and lost 10.9%. Every predictor or stall-hiding idea since
r6 has lost because it added load to this wall, so a zero-CPI change that takes one source
out of all twelve EX operand muxes is the structural lever left.
