derived from the ID word:
1. EX/MEM: replace ld_hx / ld_wx / ld_s[3:0] by two registered one-hot
   sign-select nibbles computed from the existing agu_sum[1:0]/width/sext
   decode: sw[3:0] = ld_s (signed byte or half; feeds [31:16]) and
   sh[3:0] = ld_s & {4{byte}} (signed byte only; feeds [15:8]). Net +2 flops.
2. MEM: build the sign as two shared half nets computed once next to the
   BSRAM, sA = sw[0]&DO[7] | sw[1]&DO[15], sB = sw[2]&DO[23] | sw[3]&DO[31]
   (and hA/hB likewise on sh), one LUT4 each, so every DO sign pin gains
   exactly one load (r10s2/r12s0: count DO pin loads). Then
     load_data[31:16][n] = (ld_w & DO[n]) | sA | sB          (one LUT4)
     load_data[15:8][n]  = (h0 & DO[n]) | (h2 & DO[n+16]) | hA | hB
   where the [15:8] term is the existing lane LUT4 OR-ed with hA|hB; let
   synthesis pack it (LUT4 + MUX2_LUT5 is fine, the MUX is a dedicated fast
   cell). No syn_keep on sA/sB/hA/hB so Gowin may absorb them into the
   bit LUTs if it finds a shorter mapping. This removes the separate
   ld_sign -> fill LUT level: DO -> half-sign LUT -> bit LUT -> ID merge
   LUT (3 levels, same as the byte lanes) instead of 4.
3. Nothing else changes: id_stage's merge (hit_m ? m_nl : old) |
   (hit_m & m_ld_data), the w_q port, forwarding, decode, PC/stall cones
   are untouched; CPI is identical (cycles must stay exactly 4,251,815
   with --istall --dstall; check in cosim before synthesis).
Expected: ~0.35-0.45 ns off the DO -> ID cone (7.92 ns period). Because
r12s1 showed other cones (b_val -> ALU -> oth_q, dmem_ready stall -> PC,
shifter) within ~0.3 ns, the implementer must run `make timing` and record
all three placement options' Fmax and top-10 paths for the champion and
for this change; if after the cut a second DO-derived cone (e.g. DO ->
MEM/WB.result or DO -> rs1/b_val merges) or the r12s1 b_val -> oth_q cone
is now worst by < 0.2 ns, report it in implementation_notes instead of
bundling a second cut (r14s0 lesson: one cut per slot).

lesson: - 2026-10-01 hyp-20261001-001-r15s0 (regression, -3.56%): Making r14s0's load-sign cut alone and function-identical on r11s1 (ld_hx/ld_wx/ld_s replaced by registered one-hot sign nibbles sw/sh, with four shared half-sign LUTs sgn_a/b and sgh_a/b OR-ed straight into the [31:16]/[15:8] bit LUTs, no syn_keep) scored 286.26, which at the unchanged 4,251,815 cycles means ~121.7 MHz against 126.2 (+0.29 ns where the plan predicted -0.35 to -0.45 ns; as in r12s0 and r14s0, the per-option split and top-10 paths that the plan required were not logged), so a sign-fill rewrite alone costs about as much as r14s0's whole bundle (~120.2 MHz), which likely makes r14s0's sf_h/sf_w sign cut the main culprit there too; both rewrites removed a LUT level on paper but split the champion's single shared ld_sign net, so each of DO[7/15/23/31] drives two sign LUTs instead of one and four sign nets fan out to the 24 fill bits where one did, and ~121.7 MHz is also r12s1's median (options 1/2), whose worst path was b_val -> ALU -> oth_q, so the re-placement may simply have exposed that cone; so treat r11s1's load align (one shared ld_sign net, one sign-LUT load per DO pin, select flops from EX) as a local optimum, do not use LUT-level counts as a proxy for Fmax on the DO -> ID bypass, and spend no more slots on this cone unless the implementer logs all three placement options' paths for both the champion and the change.

title: Cascaded late ALU in MEM: load/MUL consumers (add/sub/logic, store data) issue with no bubble and read the producer from the w_q flop
motivation:
After r11s1 (296.83, ~126.2 MHz, 4,251,815 cycles) the cycle budget is
roughly: ~773K imem-stall bubbles, ~208K load-use + ~36K MUL-use bubbles,
~150K dmem-stall holds and ~69K control bubbles (log.jsonl motivations of
r12s2/r13s0/r13s2). Branch prediction is exhausted (r13s0: all control
bubbles are ~1.6%), load-address prediction does not work on CoreMark
(r12s2: -0.27%), and every core-side fetch/word buffer at the fetch/ID
boundary has lost Fmax (r6s1, r8s1, r13s1, r14s1, r14s2). The load/MUL-use
interlock (~244K cycles, ~5.7%) is the largest bucket that has not been
attacked structurally. Its producer value already exists in a plain
fabric flop one cycle after MEM: MEM/WB.result (w_q), which holds the
load data or the DSP product of the instruction that just left MEM.
A consumer that sits exactly one slot behind a LOAD/MUL reaches MEM in
exactly the cycle w_q holds that value, so it can do its arithmetic
there instead of in EX — the "late ALU" of SiFive's U7 / Cortex-A55-style
load pipes — without any new path from the dmem DO or the DSP outputs.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a small second ALU in MEM (add/sub + AND/OR/XOR, no shifter, no
compare) whose "late" operand is the w_q flop, and let an eligible
consumer of a LOAD/MUL (or of another late op) enter EX with no bubble.

ID (decode, registered):
  * e1/e2 = eligibility of the raw ID word per operand: OP/OP-IMM
    ADD/ADDI/SUB/AND/OR/XOR(+I) (funct7 != M) for rs1/rs2; STORE for rs2
    only (store data); everything else (branches, JALR, load/store
    address, shifts, SLT*, M-ext) is not eligible.
  * late_a / late_b = ID/EX.lu_arm && ID/EX.rd == rs1/rs2 && e1/e2
    (the same compares hazard_unit already does). For a late operand the
    EX forward select is forced to rf (EX/MEM fwd of a LOAD/MUL is 0
    anyway) so ID/EX.rs?_val holds the correct pre-producer value for the
    misaligned-load trap case.
  * load_use_hazard = lu_arm && ((rd==rs1 && !e1) || (rd==rs2 && !e2)):
    e1/e2 depend only on opcode/funct bits, so they settle in parallel
    with the 5-bit compares and merge into the existing final LUT.
  * lu_arm of the consumer is set when it is itself late (rd != 0), so a
    chain of eligible ops after a load (lh; add; sh — matrix_add_const;
    mul; add — matrix_mul inner loops; lbu; addi; andi) runs late
    back-to-back with zero bubbles, and the first non-eligible consumer
    takes the single bubble the load would have caused.
  * a late op clears its EX result-group selects (add_q/oth_q = 0).
EX: latches the non-late operand (rs1_val, rs2_val already in EX/MEM;
    add an imm/b copy from the ID/EX b_val FLOP, not from EX nets, so no
    wall net in EX gains a consumer), plus late_a/late_b/lop/sub bits.
MEM: la = (late_a && wq_w_en) ? wq_result : rs1_val; lb likewise
    (imm when alu_src); late_out = one-hot-gated (la +/- lb | la op lb),
    OR-ed into nl_result / result as a 4th term of the existing LUT4 merge
    (mul | add_q | oth_q | late). Store data: dmem_wdata takes wq_result
    when late_d (before the byte replication). wq_w_en in the select makes
    a trapping (non-writing) producer fall back to the old value.
MEM/WB.result gets CE = !stall_ex_mem so a late STORE held by a dmem
    stall keeps its producer value (the only new load on the stall net:
    32 CE pins; if that costs Fmax, drop store-data eligibility instead).
Correctness argument: a late op is marked only when ID/EX captures it,
which requires !stall_id (so !dmem_stall: its producer moves EX->MEM on
the same edge), and a non-memory op in EX/MEM can never be bubbled out
from under it (ex_busy only bubbles a DIV, which is not eligible), so the
late op's MEM cycle is always the cycle after its producer's completed MEM
cycle, i.e. w_q holds exactly the producer's result.

Timing: the new path is flop (w_q / EX/MEM) -> 2:1 LUT -> 32-bit carry
chain -> LUT4 merge -> ID bypass LUT -> ID/EX, all from fabric flops,
i.e. carry + 3 LUTs, shorter than the champion's wall path dmem DO
(BSRAM clk-to-out) -> align -> merge -> bypass. The interlock gains only
parallel decode on the ID word (one possible extra input on the final
hazard LUT). Nothing touches take/br_lt_v, the PC mux, fetch_pred or the
regfile read addresses.

Gate before synthesis (cosim --istall --dstall is cycle-exact): count
removed load/MUL-use bubbles; build only if cycles drop >= 4% (<= ~4.08M).
My estimate is 100-170K of the ~244K bubbles (matrix MUL->add chains,
load->add->store chains, state-machine lbu->addi), i.e. -2.5% to -4%
cycles, so this needs Fmax to hold at r11s1's ~126 MHz.

lesson: - 2026-10-01 hyp-20261001-002-r15s1 (regression, -30.26%): A MEM-stage late ALU (add/sub/AND/OR/XOR on the w_q flop, so an eligible LOAD/MUL consumer or store-data operand enters EX with no bubble and late ops re-arm lu_arm to chain) scored 207.01, the largest regression logged so far; since fitness = Fmax*1e7/cycles and the late ALU can only remove bubbles, that is <= ~88.0 MHz even at the unchanged 4,251,815 cycles (~84.5 MHz at its <= 4.08M gate) against r11s1's 126.2, a >= 3.4 ns loss where the plan expected a "carry chain + 3 LUTs" path shorter than the DO wall (the cosim bubble counts, split and timing_paths were not logged); the likely cause is that every piece of a load-use bypass in this 4-stage core lands on an existing wall cone: the ~12-bit opcode/funct3/funct7 eligibility decode on the raw ID word feeds the final LUT of the imem word -> load-use hazard -> stall_id -> PC-hold/ID-EX CE cone (r12s0: ID-word-derived selects are already on the wall), MEM/WB.result gained 32 CE pins on the dmem_ready stall net (r10s0's fragile net), a 32-bit carry chain became a term of nl_result in front of r11s1's last-select MEM->ID bypass, and l_b was latched from EX's post-forward rs2 net (which also drives the branch compare) despite the plan's own "only from ID/EX flops" rule; since the plan's 2.5-4% cycle cut buys only ~0.2-0.33 ns of period at 7.92 ns, any interlock-removal scheme must first price each new load on the ID word, the stall net and the post-forward operand nets separately (r14s1: these costs add per cone) and fit them all into that budget.

title: Two-ahead pipelined fetch-word predictor: BSRAM word table read on a flop-predicted PC, used only on imem-stall cycles
motivation:
Branch prediction is used up as a lever: r12s2/r13s0 measured all control
bubbles at ~69K (~1.6%) of r11s1's 4,251,815 cycles. The only large cost
left is imem-ready stalls, ~0.8M cycles (~18%): 2.92M instructions retire
and the bus delivers <= 0.78 words/cycle. Word prediction is proven as CPI:
r14s1 (2K-entry cache) reached 3,633,187 cycles (-14.5%) and r14s2 (64-entry
word table, blocked after EX branches) reached 3,806,867 (-10.5%). Both lost
only on Fmax, and their logged worst paths show why. r14s1's path was
cq_word -> ID mux -> hazard -> hold -> u_bp idx_q (10 cells), because a hold
term steered the cache address and use_c needed a 30-bit pc compare at use
time. r14s2's path was u_if/pc -> pcn carry chain -> 64-deep table read ->
tag compare -> use_h_q (19 cells, 17.1 ns), because the whole lookup ran in
ONE cycle starting from the PC. Neither paid only the single LUT on the ID
word that the scheme really needs. In the timed wrapper io_imemData and
io_imemReady are flops (core_bench_si.sv: LFSR / bench_stall_gen), so a
flop-vs-flop LUT4 select on the ID word is the minimum price (~0.4-0.5 ns,
r6s1), and the lookup itself can be pipelined.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add rtl/fetch_word.sv, a word predictor whose lookup spans two flop-to-flop
cycles, so the only change in front of ID is one LUT4 per word bit on flops.
  Stage A (cycle t-1), predict PC(t+1) two fetches ahead from flops plus
  fetch_pred's DO. pcn_d = pc_inc + inc_d, with pc_inc = IF's existing
  pc[31:2] + inc_q and inc_d = fetch_pred's next inc_q D value (hit && !jump
  ? sext(off) : 1). Add a carry chain after the predictor DO and take a
  syn_keep'd copy of pc_inc so the PC loop nets gain no load. pcn_d feeds
  the word-table BSRAM address directly (absorbed ADB register, as for the
  imem). Add pv_q <= !stall_if && !id_ex.ctrl.is_jump && !id_ex.br_ok, which
  is one extra load on the raw stall_if / kill-bit nets. NO hold mux on any
  address, no take / br_lt_v / jalr_go / agu consumer.
  Stage B (cycle t), BSRAM word table, 256 x {v, tag pc[19:10], word}, about
  2 BSRAMs. DO goes straight into cw_q[31:0]. use_q <= v && tag ==
  pcn_q[19:10] && pv_q && !stall_if && !id_ex.ctrl.is_jump && !id_ex.br_ok:
  the PC really advanced by inc at t-1 and t, and no branch, JALR, p_bad or
  unpredicted JAL is in EX that could redirect. This is r14s2's
  register-sourced blk rule, so take gets no new consumer.
  Stage C (cycle t+1). ID word = (use_q && !io_imemReady) ? cw_q :
  io_imemData, one LUT4 per bit on flops, with 4 syn_preserve use_q copies
  capped at about 16 loads each. The bus word always wins when it arrives,
  so formal (imem always ready) never sees the table. hazard imem_stall =
  !imem_ready && !use_q, which folds into the existing stall_if LUT tree.
  IF/ID valid = imem_ready | use_q.
Fill: register {pc, io_imemData} of every delivered fetch for one cycle and
write it at pc[9:2] from flops only. A store in MEM, registered one cycle,
invalidates its index and has priority on the write port. FENCE.I is legal
as a NOP, but CoreMark never writes code. The table only replaces bus
bubbles, so a wrong-but-tagged word is impossible: the tag and the two-step
path-validity bits prove the word is for the current PC.
Required cosim gate before synthesis: run --istall --dstall and log
covered-stall, use_q-killed (pv / blk / stall) and miss counters. Ship only
if cycles <= 3.90M (-8.3%). At r6s1's one-LUT price (~119 MHz), 3.90M cycles
gives ~+3.5% and 3.80M gives ~+6%. If the gate fails because of pv losses
after holds, add `pcn_d = hold ? pc_inc : pc_inc + inc_d` on the 8 index
bits only, and measure that variant separately.
Log the per-option Fmax split and the top timing_paths for all three
placement options.

Instantiate fetch_word; wire inc_d, pc_inc copy, stall_if, ID/EX is_jump/br_ok kill bits, EX/MEM store address/valid, imem ready/data and cw_q/use_q into IF and hazard_unit.

lesson: - 2026-10-01 hyp-20261001-003-r15s2 (regression, -5.77%): A two-ahead pipelined word predictor (256-entry BSRAM table addressed from pc + inc_q + fetch_pred's next inc, registered cw_q/use_q, ID word = `imem_ready ? imem_data : fw_word`, imem_stall = !imem_ready && !use_q) obeyed every rule from r14s1/r14s2 (no hold on the table address, lookup split over two flop-to-flop cycles, use only as a flop) and shrank their -13.0%/-22.6% to -5.77%, yet 279.69 still means ~118.9 MHz even with no cycle cut (the plan's own one-LUT price) and ~109 MHz at its 3.90M cosim gate (+0.5 to +1.2 ns against r11s1's 7.92 ns; the cycles/Fmax split was not available), so the "one LUT4 on flops" premise and the 8% cycle cut cannot both have held; the likely structural cause is that any select where the bus word wins must put io_imemReady into all 32 ID-word LUTs, and in r11s1 that wrapper flop has exactly one load (hazard imem_stall, the head of the stall_if -> hold -> PC/fetch_pred cone), so this mux (like r14s1's identical one) takes that net from fanout 1 to ~33+ plus fetch_word's own loads, a cost that pipelining the lookup cannot remove and that the plan's capped use_q copies never touched; with r6s1, r8s1, r13s1, r14s1, r14s2 and r15s2 all losing (-1.9% to -22.6%), treat core-side word sources at the fetch/ID boundary as closed unless a design keeps io_imemReady at its single hazard load and cosim first shows a cycle cut that pays for a ~1 ns loss.
